timeline:
Date/Timestamp: 2020-02-03
Value: CPO 645.85 USD/tonne; PKO 840.00 USD/tonne
Textual Content:
Supply: Oil World projects global palm oil output to decline by 1 million tonne in the 2019/2020 season, setting the stage for a second consecutive annual supply deficit and resulting in unusually small stocks at season-end.
Demand: Steady global demand for palm oil, with increased edible oil imports by China. The Indonesian Embassy in Phnom Penhn, Cambodia, held a "Morning Tea Discussion: Palm Oil for Healthy Life" on January 29 to promote palm oil's health benefits, reaching Cambodian officials' wives, ambassadors' wives, and members of the Cambodian Women Entrepreneur Association (CWEA). The coronavirus outbreak, which has killed over 360 people and spread to over 17,000, led to China's isolation, with countries like the U.S., India, Australia, Indonesia, Singapore, Israel, Russia, New Zealand, and the Philippines imposing visitor restrictions from China. This implied a reduction in Chinese CPO consumption. Chinese officials urged investors to objectively evaluate the virus impact, while China expects to be a big buyer in world meat markets due to the virus and pre-existing need.
Policy & Trade: India's Finance Ministry issued a notification stating a 44% import tax on crude palm oil (CPO). However, trade sources, including Sudhakar Desai (president of the Indian Vegetable Oil Producers’ Association), clarified that the import duty under the ASEAN free trade agreement remains unchanged at 37.5%. The 44% rate applies to cargoes that do not enjoy origin-benefits in India. India had previously slashed CPO duties from ASEAN to 37.5% (from 40%) and refined palm oil to 45% (from 50%) starting this year. India relies on imports for 70% of its edible oil requirements, with Indonesia and Malaysia supplying almost two-thirds of its annual 15 million tonnes.
Substitutes & Energy: Vegetable oil markets are supported by dwindling rapeseed supplies due to poor harvests in the European Union and Australia. The soybean market is less supported, anticipating a bumper Brazilian harvest, higher U.S. production, and uncertain Chinese demand, as swine fever reduced the need for soy protein in pig feed, but limited soybean oil supply from crushing led China to import more edible oil. U.S. soybeans edged up 0.2% to $8.74-1/2 a bushel after hitting a two-month low of $8.70-3/4. Corn futures were down 0.3% at $3.80-1/4, and wheat futures were down 0.9% at $5.48-3/4. Oil prices extended declines due to worries about lower demand in China. Private exporters reported the sale of 134,000 tonnes of corn to South Korea for the 2019/20 marketing year. March soymeal futures closed $1.20 per short ton lower at $289.80, and March soy oil futures settled $0.35 cents higher at 30.29 cents per pound.
Market & Technicals: Chinese stocks (CSI 300 Index) plummeted 9.1% as markets reopened after the Lunar New Year. China’s benchmark iron ore, copper, crude, and palm oil also sank by their daily maximum allowed. The People’s Bank of China set the yuan fixing at 6.9249 per dollar, stronger than expected, and pledged financial stability, supplying cash to offset 1.05 trillion yuan ($152 billion) in short-term funding. Hong Kong’s Hang Seng Index slid 0.5% after dropping 5.9% last week. The Shanghai Composite Index sank 2.8% on January 23. CPO futures for April 2020 on Bursa Malaysia fell from RM 3,060 per ton on January 13 to RM 2,604 per ton on January 31. Oil World's Thomas Mielke suggested that recent price falls on Bursa Malaysia were driven by emotions and uncertainty rather than fundamentals. The U.S. dollar was higher, and the Dow Jones Industrials were 188 points higher.
Forward Views: Oil World's Thomas Mielke conservatively estimates average palm oil prices for January-June at about $800 a tonne, up from $770. He stated that if Indonesia fully implements its B30 biofuel program, prices could increase by as much as $150. Mielke believes fundamentals are bullish and likely to become more bullish in 2021. Analysts Chris Apriliony (Jasa Utama Capital Sekuritas) sees positive prospects for CPO stocks, recommending "buy" due to current low prices (though still high year-on-year). Liza Camelia Suryanata (Henan Putihrai Sekuritas) advises short-term trading, noting CPO prices are volatile and news-driven.

Date/Timestamp: 2020-02-04
Value: CPO 657.03 USD/tonne; PKO 830.00 USD/tonne
Textual Content:
Supply: Indonesia, the world's top palm oil producer, produced 47.1 million tonnes of CPO and 4.6 million tonnes of palm kernel oil in 2019, up from 43 million tonnes of CPO and 4.3 million tonnes of PKO in 2018. Indonesia's palm oil stockpiles stood at about 4.6 million tonnes at the end of 2019. Production growth in 2020 is expected to slow due to the effects of drought and reduced fertilizer usage in 2019 impacting yields (GAPKI Chairman Joko Supriyono). Malaysian palm oil stocks hit a 27-month low of 2.01 million tonnes at end-December, an 11% decline from end-November, as reported by the Malaysian Palm Oil Board. The Indonesian Biofuel Producers Association (APROBI) expects 3.62 million kiloliters (KL) of additional production capacity in 2020. Indonesia's current capacity for palm oil's fatty acid methyl ester (FAME) is 12 million KL, with practical utilization up to 85% (10 million KL). Another 3.6 million KL of capacity is expected to come online in 2021. Sabah launched its BESS brand cooking oil, produced by Benta Edible Oil Sdn Bhd, a subsidiary of Benta Wawasan Sdn Bhd, with a current production of 2,000 tons of packaged cooking oil per month. Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Panglima Mohd Shafie Apdal announced plans for another "Made in Sabah" cooking oil by Sawit Kinabalu and the development of a 200-acre (80.94-hectare) industrial area in Tawau for downstream industries like cooking oil, candle, soap, and cosmetics.
Demand: Indonesia exported a record 36.18 million tonnes of palm oil and its products (including biodiesel and oleochemical) in 2019, a 4.2% increase from 34.71 million tonnes in 2018, driven by rising demand from China, the Middle East, and African markets, which offset declines elsewhere. India recorded the biggest decline in demand due to higher import tariffs on Indonesian shipments. GAPKI is monitoring the impact of the coronavirus spread on China's palm oil demand, noting China's "pretty big" exposure. The fast-spreading coronavirus, which killed 361 in China and caused over 17,000 confirmed cases in China and 151 elsewhere, is expected to affect economic activity and demand for imports, particularly for palm oil used in food courts and catering in China, leading to reduced consumption in the near to medium term. Chinese manufacturing plants are taking extended Lunar New Year breaks, and Japan's Toyota Motor Corp and other firms announced extended plant shutdowns in China. Indonesia's domestic B30 program is expected to use around 9.6 million KL of palm-based fuel this year, leaving little room for biodiesel exports early in the year, with the earliest exports anticipated in Q2 when new capacity becomes operational. Indonesia exported 1.32 million KL of FAME in 2019, down from 1.6 million KL in 2018, partly due to EU anti-subsidy import duties. Growing demand for biodiesel was noted in China, which accounted for half of Indonesia's biodiesel exports last year. Malaysia's total trade in December 2019 recorded positive growth of 1.9% year-on-year, ending a six-month contraction streak, with exports expanding 2.7% year-on-year after four consecutive months of negative growth. BESS cooking oil is to be sold locally in Sabah at affordable prices (RM5 for a 1 kg bottle, RM9 for a 2 kg bottle, RM20 for a 5 kg bottle), with plans to market it to neighboring countries.
Policy & Trade: India's Finance Ministry issued a notification regarding a 44% import tax on CPO, but the import duty under the ASEAN free trade agreement remains 37.5%, as clarified by the Indian Vegetable Oil Producers’ Association. The 44% duty applies to non-origin benefit cargoes. Malaysia's Primary Industries Minister Teresa Kok stated that India’s move to cut back on palm oil purchases is “temporary” and will be resolved amicably. India restricted imports of refined palm oil and informally stopped all purchases from Malaysia following diplomatic tensions regarding Kashmir and a new citizenship law. Malaysia’s B20 biodiesel implementation, starting this month, is expected to help sustain high CPO prices (Malaysian Palm Oil Council). Indonesia's Coordinating Minister for Maritime Affairs and Investment Luhut Pandjaitan denied plans to ban food and beverage imports from China, contradicting earlier comments by Trade Minister Agus Suparmanto. China is Indonesia's biggest trade partner, importing coal, stainless steel, and palm oil. The Indonesian government expanded its mandatory B20 biodiesel program to B30 in late 2019 (30% FAME in biodiesel) and plans to begin testing for B40 soon. Malaysia is sending a delegation to Europe by the end of February to present its sustainable palm oil measures to counter the European Union’s progressive phase-out of palm oil by 2030 under the Renewable Energy Directive (RED II), which classifies palm oil from large plantations as unsustainable. The Deputy International Trade and Industry Minister Dr Ong Kian Ming noted that India reduced its CPO tariffs for ASEAN to 37% in 2019 due to a free-trade agreement but stated the tariff rate had recently "gone up again to about 44%", clarifying it's not targeted at Malaysia alone but other countries outside India's FTAs. Malaysia decided in March 2019 to cap oil palm plantation expansion to 6.5 million hectares (from 5.85 million hectares in 2018), restricting peatland development and banning conversion of permanent forest reserves for palm oil. Malaysia aims to have all its palm plantations certified sustainable by the end of 2020, with 60% of total oil palm area already Malaysian Sustainable Palm Oil (MSPO) certified, targeting 70% by end-February. The Chief Minister of Sabah is awaiting subsidy approval from the Domestic Trade and Consumer Affairs Ministry for BESS cooking oil, which could reduce prices by up to 30%.
Substitutes & Energy: OPEC and its allies are discussing bringing forward a policy meeting to this month from March to consider deepening oil supply curbs by an additional 500,000 bpd to 2.2 million bpd due to the virus hitting oil demand. China's Sinopec Corp is cutting throughput by 600,000 bpd (about 12%), its steepest cut in over a decade. Sinopec's trading arm Unipec has suspended purchases of West African crude and is re-selling at least five March-loading Angolan cargoes. Analysts predict China's oil demand could fall by 250,000 bpd in Q1 2020, with jet fuel demand hardest hit. Jet fuel prices and production margins in Asia recorded their biggest monthly decline in over a decade in January. Oil prices have fallen to their lowest since last January. CME Group’s March soybean futures ended 4 1/4¢ higher at $8.77, and May soybean futures settled 4¢ higher at $8.90 3/4. March corn futures finished 2 1/2¢ lower at $3.78 3/4, and May corn futures settled 2¢ lower at $3.84 3/4. March wheat futures finished 1 3/4¢ higher at $5.55 1/2. NYMEX crude oil market was $1.43 per barrel lower. Concerns were raised about singleing out palm oil for deforestation while ignoring other crops like soy.
Market & Technicals: Dalian palm oil futures plunged by their daily limit of 7% on Monday as trading resumed. Malaysia’s benchmark palm oil contract for April delivery plunged 14.9% in January, its biggest monthly drop since August 2014. On Monday, the contract was up 1.2% at 2,634 ringgit per tonne after dropping nearly 9% last week. Prices had climbed 46.7% from Oct 1 to Jan 6 to three-year highs of 3,133 ringgit a tonne. Brokers are taking on more short positions, with open interest across all Malaysia palm oil contracts growing by roughly 30,000 contracts in January. Palm oil prices steadied on Monday (in ringgit terms) after two straight sessions of losses. Shanghai copper prices dived to a three-year low, and other Shanghai-traded industrial metals also tumbled. Asian shares were gripped by a fragile calm. U.S. stocks rallied on Monday, boosted by technology shares and surprising strength in U.S. manufacturing activity. RHB Investment Bank Bhd economist Ahmad Nazmi Idrus noted support from better palm oil prices in recent months for Malaysian exports. As of Monday, 3.87 million hectares (66.22% of total 5.85 million hectares plantation areas) have obtained Malaysian Sustainable Palm Oil (MSPO) certification, with 88.76% of organized smallholders and 10.17% of independent smallholders certified. The U.S. dollar was higher.
Forward Views: Brokers and traders expect Malaysian palm oil futures to fall below 2,500 ringgit over coming weeks if the coronavirus spread continues to disrupt travel and activity in China. Five traders expect palm oil to fall to between 2,470 and 2,575 ringgit a tonne within coming weeks. Paramalingam Supramaniam (Pelindung Bestari Sdn Bhd) stated the market would remain bearish until fresh demand emerges. RHB Investment Bank economist Ahmad Nazmi Idrus expects Malaysia's export growth to remain around 1.5% for 2020, with a possible upside revision. MIDF Research forecasts 1.5% year-on-year export growth for 2020, expecting commodity-based sectors (liquefied natural gas, crude palm oil) to perform well. The Deputy International Trade and Industry Minister Dr Ong Kian Ming expects Malaysia’s total trade to reach RM2 trillion in 2020, targeting a 2.0% increase in both import and export, based on anticipated recovery in global economic environment and improving commodity prices. He expressed cautious optimism for palm oil exports to India in 2020. Reuters analyst Wang Tao stated palm oil is biased to break a support at 2,592 ringgit per tonne and fall into a range of 2,435-2,513 ringgit.

Date/Timestamp: 2020-02-05
Value: CPO 689.40 USD/tonne; PKO 875.00 USD/tonne
Textual Content:
Supply: Malaysian palm oil futures rose over 2% (April delivery contract touched 2,687 ringgit/tonne, highest since Thursday, then 0.8% higher at 2,635 ringgit/$640.34 per tonne) due to expected decline in January production (forecast 4% to 17%, or even 22%). Dry weather and lower fertilizer use reduced output last year and are likely to continue affecting production this year. Kuala Lumpur decided in March 2019 to cap oil palm plantation expansion to 6.5 million hectares (up from 5.85 million hectares in 2018), restricting peatland development, banning conversion of permanent forest reserves for palm oil, and producing an official map of plantations. Malaysia aims for all its palm plantations to be certified sustainable by end-2020, with 60% already Malaysian Sustainable Palm Oil (MSPO) certified, targeting 70% by end-February. The Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil (RSPO) has certified 13 million tonnes (21% of world's supply) as responsible and sustainable, but only half of this is sold due to low demand.
Demand: Pakistan is ready to import more palm oil from Malaysia, with Prime Minister Imran Khan pledging to try his best to compensate for India's reduced imports. Malaysia’s total exports of palm oil and its downstream derivatives for January-November last year stood at 25.7 million tonnes, an increase of 10.9% from 23.2 million tonnes in the same period in 2018. Palm oil generated an income of more than RM59 billion to Malaysia during this period, a decline of 5.9% compared to RM62.7 billion in 2018. Major palm oil export destinations for Malaysia include China, India, the EU, the US, and Japan. The food industry consumes about 70% of the world's palm oil supply. The world palm oil market is estimated at €55 billion ($60 billion) and is expected to reach €80 billion by 2021. Concerns about China's coronavirus outbreak and its impact on demand capped gains in palm oil prices. The coronavirus death toll spiked to 425, with over 20,000 confirmed cases in China. WWF's Palm Oil Buyers Scorecard (January 17) shows that consumer goods companies are falling short in supporting sustainable palm oil production; only 10 out of 53 Consumer Goods Forum (CGF) members scored in the top 10% for sustainability efforts, with nearly a quarter making no commitments.
Policy & Trade: India restricted refined palm oil and palm olein imports, requiring importers to apply for licenses, following remarks by Malaysian Prime Minister Dr Mahathir Mohamad regarding India's actions in Kashmir and its new citizenship law. Malaysian Primary Industries Minister Teresa Kok stated that the B20 biodiesel mandate, implemented this month, is expected to help sustain high crude palm oil prices. Indonesia's Coordinating Minister for Maritime Affairs and Investment Luhut Pandjaitan denied plans to ban food and beverage imports from China, refuting earlier comments by Trade Minister Agus Suparmanto. China was reportedly unhappy with these ban comments, threatening equal measures. China is Indonesia's biggest trade partner, importing coal, stainless steel, and palm oil. Malaysia is sending a delegation to Europe by the end of February to present its newly adopted measures for sustainable palm oil production, aiming to circumvent a progressive European Union phase-out of palm oil by 2030. Deputy International Trade and Industry Minister Dr Ong Kian Ming noted that India reduced its CPO tariffs for ASEAN to 37% in 2019 due to a free-trade agreement, but the tariff rate had recently "gone up again to about 44%", clarifying that this is not targeted at Malaysia alone but for other countries outside India’s free-trade agreements.
Substitutes & Energy: Gains in rival oils supported palm oil prices, with Dalian palm oil rising 2% and soyoil trading 1.3% higher after declining 7% in the previous session. Chicago Board of Trade soybean oil rose 0.8%. Oil prices rose around 0.5% as investors regained some calm after Monday's sharp sell-off due to virus worries. The European biodiesel market is estimated at €9 billion per year. Concerns were raised about singling out palm oil for deforestation while ignoring other crops, such as soy grown in the Amazon.
Market & Technicals: Malaysia’s benchmark palm oil contract for April delivery on the Bursa Malaysia Derivatives Exchange rose a second straight day. The contract was last trading about 0.8% higher at 2,635 ringgit ($640.34) per tonne. Concerns about China's coronavirus outbreak and its impact on demand capped gains. Asian shares maintained a fragile calm. U.S. stocks rallied on Monday, boosted by technology shares and manufacturing activity. For Malaysia, export volume for palm oil and palm oil products increased 10.9% to 28 million tonnes in 2019, despite a 4.0% decline in export value to RM64.84 billion. India was the top export destination for palm oil and palm oil products in 2019, with trade value increasing by 43% to RM9.78 billion, followed by China (RM9.17 billion) and the Netherlands (RM4.52 billion). Malaysia's total trade contracted by 2.5% to RM1.835 trillion in 2019. The country's trade surplus widened by 11% to RM137.39 billion, the largest since 2009 and the 22nd consecutive year of surplus. China remained Malaysia's largest trading partner for 11 consecutive years, accounting for 17.2% of total trade in 2019, with trade valued at RM315.19 billion (a marginal increase of 0.2% from 2018).
Forward Views: Malaysian Primary Industries Minister Teresa Kok expects the novel coronavirus outbreak to have only a temporary impact on commodities prices, including CPO. The Malaysian Palm Oil Council (MPOC) forecasts the CPO price to average around RM2,600 to RM2,700 per tonne this year, anticipating high prices to continue due to B20 biodiesel implementation, lower CPO stocks, and decreased production. Economists expect Malaysia's export growth to remain around 1.5% for 2020, with commodity-based sectors, including CPO, expected to perform well. However, uncertainties over the trade war, loss of growth momentum in major economies, and the coronavirus outbreak are potential risk factors. The Ministry of International Trade and Industry targets Malaysia's total trade to reach RM2 trillion in 2020.

Date/Timestamp: 2020-02-06
Value: CPO 700.23 USD/tonne; PKO 875.00 USD/tonne
Textual Content:
Supply: A Reuters survey forecasts Malaysian palm oil inventories to fall 12% to 1.76 million tonnes in January from December, the lowest since June 2017. Production is likely to have dropped 9% to 1.21 million tonnes, the lowest since March 2016, primarily due to lower harvesting and milling activities during the Lunar New Year holidays, and effects of dry weather and lower fertilizer usage in the previous year. These factors are expected to suppress output in the first half of 2020. Malaysia's domestic consumption in January is estimated at 258,977 tonnes. Indonesia's Palm Oil Association (GAPKI) estimates the country will use 8.3 million tonnes of palm oil for domestic biodiesel demand this year, raising concerns about reduced amounts available for export. Indonesia's crude palm oil and palm kernel oil production hit a record 51.8 million tonnes last year, up 9.1% from 2018, despite a long drought.
Demand: Malaysian palm oil exports in January are likely to have plunged 8.2% month-on-month to 1.28 million tonnes, driven by lower purchases from India and China. Malaysia's monthly palm exports to India fell to about 40,500 tonnes in January, significantly down from 201,450 tonnes a year earlier. Exports to China also declined due to the coronavirus epidemic. Pakistan's Prime Minister Imran Khan pledged to buy more Malaysian palm oil to compensate for lost sales to India. Palm oil demand from Pakistan surged 129.7% month-on-month to 141,500 tonnes in January, compared to 61,600 tonnes in December 2019, according to SGS Malaysia Sdn Bhd. However, analysts and economists doubt Pakistan can fully compensate for India's reduced imports, noting Pakistan's edible oil consumption is around 4.50 million tonnes annually versus India's 24 million tonnes. Pakistan would need an additional 3.309 million tonnes to fully offset the loss. Market observers expect India's palm oil purchase from Malaysia to fall below 70,000 tonnes in January (compared to 253,889 tonnes in January last year) and potentially below 10,000 tonnes in February as Indian buyers shift to Indonesia. India buys over 9 million tonnes of palm oil annually, predominantly from Indonesia and Malaysia, accounting for about two-thirds of its total edible oil imports. Prices for commodities, including crude palm oil, have plunged in February due to decreasing demand from China, where the coronavirus outbreak is expected to further drag down prices. Fear over the virus is weighing on slow economic activity during the Chinese New Year holidays. Indonesia's palm oil exports to China have stopped temporarily. Indonesia is exploring increased demand in other markets, such as Africa, which imported 2.9 million tonnes of palm oil products from Indonesia last year, up 11%.
Policy & Trade: India's import duty on CPO will likely be maintained at 37.5% for ASEAN countries, despite an official notice from India's Ministry of Finance stating 44%. Industry consultant MR Chandran explained the 44% hike was intended to curb indirect palm oil imports from non-ASEAN countries (Nepal, Pakistan, Bangladesh) to India. India's Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs confirmed the 37.5% levy for ASEAN. India had slashed CPO duty from ASEAN to 37.5% (from 40%) and refined palm oil to 45% (from 50%) since January 1. India imposed restrictions on refined palm oil imports and informally ceased all palm oil purchases from Malaysia last month in response to Prime Minister Dr Mahathir Mohamad's criticism of India's policy towards Kashmir and its new citizenship laws. India’s Solvent Extractors’ Association had requested members halt imports from Malaysia. Pakistan's Prime Minister Imran Khan pledged to buy more Malaysian palm oil to offset lost sales to India. The Malaysian Palm Oil Council (MPOC) expects India’s move to be “temporary” and resolved amicably. The implementation of Malaysia's B20 biodiesel mandate this month is expected to help retain crude palm oil prices. India's External Affairs Ministry spokesman Raveesh Kumar strongly criticized the reference to Jammu and Kashmir in the Pakistan-Malaysia joint statement, calling for Malaysian leaders to acknowledge Pakistan as "an epicentre of global terrorism." PKR president Anwar Ibrahim suggested Dr Mahathir had dialed back his criticism of India. India appears positive about resuming trade of refined palm oil from Nepal, which had been halted since January 10. Nepal's exports account for a mere 1% of Indian imports. The Indonesian government began mandatory B30 use last month and is preparing for B40 next year. Malaysia's Ministry of Primary Industries is exploring new markets in the US, Europe, Africa, Iran, and China. Dr Ahmad Parveez Ghulam Kadir (MPOB director-general) applauded Pakistan's efforts, noting Primary Industries Minister Teresa Kok's visit to Pakistan last month and hoping MSPO certification will open more markets.
Substitutes & Energy: Malaysian palm oil futures tracked gains from higher rival oil prices, with Dalian's most-active soyaoil contract rising 1.8% and its palm oil contract up 2.3%. Soyaoil prices on the Chicago Board of Trade also gained 2.7%. Global rubber prices at the Tokyo Commodity Exchange have slipped around 17% so far this year. Coal prices declined around 5% over the same period. Crude palm oil prices declined around 15% over the same period.
Market & Technicals: Malaysian palm oil futures rebounded 5.1% on Wednesday, with the benchmark contract for April delivery settling up 138 ringgit at 2,804 ringgit ($681.16) per tonne, marking its third straight session of gains after tumbling almost 9% last week. The crude palm oil market appears more concerned about supply shortfall than potential demand rationing due to slower global growth from the coronavirus outbreak (Ivy Ng, CIMB Investment Bank). Some bargain buying was noted for palm oil deliveries for March to Q2 2020 (Marcello Cultrera, Phillip Futures). FGV Holdings Bhd's shares rose three sen to RM1.37 with 5.41 million shares transacted; analysts suggest FGV could benefit from increased palm oil supply to Pakistan due to its large presence and recent investment exploration in Pakistan, including an MoU to acquire up to 25% stake in Fauji Akbar Portia Marine Terminals. FGV has invested RM98.5 million in Pakistan to date. ($1 = RM4.1210). Indonesia recorded a trade deficit of $3.2 billion in 2019, an improvement from $8.7 billion in 2018. China accounted for 25.85% of Indonesia’s total non-oil and gas exports in 2019, with exports to China at $25.8 billion and imports from China at $44.5 billion, leading to an $18.7 billion trade deficit for Indonesia.
Forward Views: Sathia Varqa (Palm Oil Analytics) expressed doubt that Pakistan, even if it honors its commitment, could fully compensate for the loss of the Indian market, and foresees a significant increase only if Malaysia enjoys tariff advantages over Indonesia. Independent economist Hoo Ke Peng cited Pakistan’s external debt and liabilities of US$106.9 billion in Q1, questioning its financial capacity for additional imports. Ahamed Kameel Mydin Meera suggested a netting arrangement (Malaysia buying rice/meat from Pakistan, with Pakistan paying the balance after buying palm oil). The Ministry of International Trade and Industry in Malaysia reiterated its target of RM2 trillion for total trade in 2020, assuming improving global economic situation and commodity prices.

Date/Timestamp: 2020-02-07
Value: CPO 691.66 USD/tonne; PKO 860.00 USD/tonne
Textual Content:
Supply: The Indonesian Palm Oil Association (Gapki) executive director Mukti Sardjono stated that Indonesia is likely to use 8.3 million tonnes of palm oil to meet domestic demand for biodiesel this year, raising concerns about insufficient palm oil available for export. Indonesia's crude palm oil and palm kernel oil production hit a record 51.8 million tonnes last year, up 9.1% from 2018, despite a long drought.
Demand: Malaysia postponed its biggest palm oil conference, POC2020, from March 2-4 to June due to the spread of the Wuhan, China coronavirus, which has also delayed over two dozen trade fairs and conferences in Asia. China is the second-largest buyer of palm oil after India. Edible oil prices in India fell up to 10% in January, partly due to an 18% drop in crude palm oil prices in Malaysia and Indonesia. Stalled palm oil supply due to the coronavirus outbreak in China has suppressed prices of other oils like soybean, rapeseed, and rice bran, after they had increased 30-40% year-on-year in Q3 of the financial year. Pakistan's Prime Minister Imran Khan pledged to buy more Malaysian palm oil to compensate for India's restrictions. Malaysia's January 2020 palm oil export to Pakistan was 141,500 tonnes, higher than the usual monthly volume of 90,500 tonnes. However, Sathia Varqa (Palm Oil Analytics) doubts Pakistan can consume enough to compensate for the 2.156 million tonnes of refined, bleached, and deodorized (RBD) palm olein lost to India, given Pakistan's edible oil consumption of around 4.50 million tonnes annually compared to India's 24 million tonnes. China was Indonesia's largest CPO and kernel palm oil market, buying 6 million tonnes in 2019, ahead of India (4.8 million tonnes) and the EU (4.6 million tonnes). China was also the biggest buyer of Indonesian oleochemical and biodiesel products, purchasing 825,000 tonnes. All Indonesian export activities to China have been temporarily stopped due to the coronavirus outbreak. Indonesia's palm oil exports gained 4% to 36.2 million tonnes in 2019, despite the US-China trade war, India's tariff discrimination, and the EU's biodiesel ban. Indonesia is looking to Africa as a market, which imported 2.9 million tonnes of palm oil products from Indonesia in 2019, up 11%.
Policy & Trade: India's External Affairs Ministry spokesman Raveesh Kumar strongly criticized the reference to Jammu and Kashmir in a Pakistan-Malaysia joint statement, calling for Malaysian leaders to acknowledge Pakistan as "an epicentre of global terrorism." India had earlier summoned Malaysia's charge d’affaires in December over Prime Minister Dr Mahathir's "insensitive" comments on India's new citizenship law. India, the world's biggest buyer of edible oils, last month imposed curbs on refined palm oil imports and informally asked traders to stop buying from Malaysia. India appears positive about resuming trade of refined palm oil from Nepal, which had been halted since January 10. Nepal's palm oil exports account for a mere 1% of Indian imports. The Indonesian government began mandatory B30 use last month and is preparing for B40 next year. Dr Ahmad Parveez Ghulam Kadir (MPOB director-general) applauded Pakistan's effort to buy more palm oil, crediting Primary Industries Minister Teresa Kok's visit to Pakistan last month. He hopes mandatory Malaysian Sustainable Palm Oil (MSPO) certification will open more markets. A Malaysian delegation led by Teresa Kok recently visited Port Qasim to assess a joint venture (FGV Holdings Bhd, IOI Corp Bhd, Kuala Lumpur Kepong Bhd with Westbury Group of Pakistan) involving bulking storage, refinery, liquid cargo jetty, and oilseed extraction. Another bulk commodities storage project (138,000 tonnes capacity) is expected to be commissioned in June 2020. This JV terminal handles 50% of palm oil imports into Pakistan. The ministry is exploring new markets in the United States, Europe, Africa, Iran, and China. Sathia Varqa suggested that Malaysia and Pakistan enter a special preferential tariff agreement for Malaysia to increase its market share over Indonesia, which holds 70% of Pakistan's olein market compared to Malaysia's 30%.
Market & Technicals: FGV Holdings Bhd's shares rose three sen to RM1.37 with 5.41 million shares transacted, potentially benefiting from a rise in palm oil supply to Pakistan due to its large presence and planned investments in the country. FGV has invested RM98.5 million in Pakistan. Export value of Indonesia's palm oil products, including oleochemicals and biodiesel, declined to $19 billion last year, down 17% from $23 billion in 2018. The CPO price recovered after President Joko Widodo announced an increase in domestic CPO use for biodiesel, closing at $800 per tonne in Rotterdam at the end of last year, almost twice the August price, as Indonesia began using the B30 mandate.
Forward Views: Gapki's Mukti Sardjono hopes the coronavirus outbreak will not last too long.

Date/Timestamp: 2020-02-10
Value: CPO 673.74 USD/tonne; PKO 845.00 USD/tonne
Textual Content:
- **Supply:** FGV Holdings Bhd expects low production from January to March but anticipates overall positive FFB growth of 2-4% year-on-year (y-o-y) for FY2020, with 4-6% CPO output growth from improved oil extraction rates and new mill/estate standards. United Malacca Bhd (UMB) will begin planting stevia (100ha initially, 5,000ha total), coconut (10,000ha), and cocoa (3,000ha) in Sulawesi, Indonesia, in FY20/21. UMB commissioned a new 45-tonne palm oil mill in Kalimantan in June 2019. Kenanga Research forecasts UMB's FY20 FFB production at 406,000 tonnes, up 11% y-o-y, driven by Indonesia (20-25% growth). Pakistan's Ministry of National Food Security and Research hopes for higher production of mustard, sunflower, canola, safflower, custard, and olives.

Substitutes & Energy: Dalian's most-active soyoil contract traded down 0.03% on Thursday, while its palm oil contract also fell 0.61%. Soyoil prices on the Chicago Board of Trade were up 0.03%. Igwe Anthony Uche, President of the Palm Growers Association of Nigeria, stated that Nigeria's palm oil deficit could be closed in four years with the help of the Central Bank's N30 billion intervention fund, in contrast to the 10-year estimate by Dr. Celestine Ikuenobe of NIFOR. The FAO food price index averaged 180.5 points in February, down 1.0% on January. The vegetable oil price index plunged 10.3% from January, led by a slump in palm oil prices. Date/Timestamp: 2020-03-09

- International edible oil prices have reduced by up to 25% due to a fall in demand from China, a major market. Indonesian exports to China (19% of its total production) are severely affected.
- Hopes of demand improving ahead of the Muslim holy month of Ramadan partially supported a weekly gain in palm oil futures.
- Long-term, as the world population grows, demand for vegetable oils in food, biofuel, and industrial uses is expected to increase.

- The European Union (EU) is in the process of phasing out palm oil in biofuels, which will pressure imports into the region.

Substitutes & Energy:

- Argentinian soybean oil shipments are projected at 6 million tonnes in 2020, up 14% year-on-year, though export taxes may impact total volumes.
- Brazil expects a stronger harvest, but higher domestic demand is expected to reduce vegoil export volumes.

- Gibson expects palm oil volumes shipped on IMO3 MRs to decline in 2020 from 8 million tonnes in 2019.

- Brazil's soy exports are expected to gather pace in southern ports as the weather turns drier.

- Palm oil gained 5.7% last week as demand from Africa and the Middle East picked up ahead of the Muslim holy month of Ramadan, countering fears over the impact of the coronavirus epidemic.

Dalian's most-active soyaoil contract traded 3.97% lower, while its palm oil contract fell 4.96%.

Daily palm oil prices (in MYR) fell almost 10% to RM2,274 per tonne at midday, the lowest since October.

Date/Timestamp: 2020-03-11

Textual Content:
Supply:

- CPO production in February jumped 9.99% (or 10%) from January to 1.29 million tonnes, marking the first increase in five months, as oil palm trees recovered from prolonged stress due to dry weather last year (Adrian Kok, Kenanga Investment Bank).

Only 19% of the world's palm oil crops are Certified Sustainable Palm Oil.

Demand:

- The newly-appointed Malaysian Plantation Industries and Commodities Minister, Datuk Dr Mohd Khairuddin Aman Razali, stated that the ministry will explore new palm oil markets to avoid over-reliance on traditional markets such as India, China, and European Union countries.
- Muted demand for edible oils in China and elsewhere due to the coronavirus is challenging producers trying to offset subsidies with palm oil export revenue.

Policy & Trade:

He also plans to build a strong team to meet challenges in the plantation and commodity sectors, such as product discrimination and anti-palm oil campaigns internationally.
- Malaysia plans to fully implement its B20 biodiesel program in the transport industry by mid-2021, and this will proceed as planned in an effort to reduce greenhouse gas emissions (Ravi Muthayah, secretary-general at the commodities ministry), despite the plunge in oil prices.

The Indonesian government, which restored a US$50 per tonne levy on crude palm oil (CPO) exports in January, plans to raise the duty as palm's premium over gasoil widens, which boosts costs for exporters.

Substitutes & Energy:

- Brent crude closed at $35.79 and WTI at $32.98.

Market & Technicals:

- The Johor state government is implementing measures to boost tourism amid a sluggish economy and Covid-19, including redistributing tourism tax receipts to companies and holding state government programs and events in major hotels. Health monitoring efforts at the land border checkpoints with Singapore will continue.

Forward Views:

- Rabobank analyst Oscar Tjakra predicts long-run investments in new and additional biofuel production capacities could be delayed if crude prices continue to remain low, as they may not be economically viable.
- Bloomberg Intelligence analyst Alvin Tai estimates that Indonesia's biodiesel fund might survive another six months before needing to start collecting more levies to keep the program going.
- Scientists recommend that chemical engineers continue to identify the necessary steps to scale up the production of the most promising microbial oils as the best palm oil replacements.
- The Energy Information Administration (EIA) expects second-quarter prices for Brent crude to be $37/bbl, rising to $42/bbl in the second half of the year.
- An acrylates buyer noted a generally pessimistic mood among intermediate producers, with most seeing markets down in the months ahead, except for the paint sector (expected flat to a little better).
- Jagran English reported that edible oil prices in India may come down by more than 10%, and wholesale prices (including palm oil, which increased 35% in December) may fall by 10-15% in the next few months, providing relief to the central government.

Date/Timestamp: 2020-03-12

Supply:

This initiative aims to ensure returns to farmers (at least ₹16,000 per tonne of oil palm with yields over 20 tonnes per acre) and allows for intermediate crops. Oil palm requires less water compared to paddy and can be cultivated through drip irrigation, also offering environmental benefits due to its high carbon dioxide absorbing nature.

The Canadian grain export system has faced challenges this winter, including a one-week Canadian National Railway strike, heavy rain in Vancouver disrupting port loading, a six-day outage of CN’s main southern line due to track washout, and track blockades. This has led to a large number of vessels waiting to be loaded at the West Coast (41 ships in Vancouver and 10 at Prince Rupert for week 30).

Demand:

Buyers typically increase purchases one or two months before Ramadan.
- China's palm oil stock still remains historically high at around 950,000 tonnes. However, once the Covid-19 epidemic wears off, consumption of edible oil is expected to resume, which could push up palm oil demand and support CPO prices.

Policy & Trade:

- India's decision not to extend the safeguard duty of 5% on certain palm oil varieties from Malaysia, which had been applied from September 2019 until early March 2020, could provide slight relief, but the positive impact is believed to be minimal due to India's existing ban on Malaysian refined palm oil (previously the majority of exports) due to political factors.
- The fall in EU palm oil exports could be a sustained trend as the EU continues its ban of palm biodiesel under the Delegated Act II and addresses the 3-monochloropropanediol (3MCPD) issue. Indonesia's Deputy Foreign Minister Mahendra Siregar reiterated that Indonesia cannot accept the EU's energy policy regarding palm oil biofuels, describing it as discriminatory and based on a narrow focus (deforestation) that ignores palm oil's higher productivity and lower fertilizer/pesticide use compared to other vegetable oils.
- The Johor state government launched a stimulus package, expanding a 50% land tax subsidy to Felda landowners who own up to 5 hectares (previously 4 hectares) of Malay reserve land in Johor.
- Angola's Credit Support Programme (PAC) and Prodesi (Program to support production, diversification of exports and import substitution) aim to increase the production of essential goods and promote import substitution, with 750 million kwanzas made available through the Angolan Development Bank (BDA) to finance agricultural cooperatives and small and medium-sized enterprises.

Substitutes & Energy:
- The demand for CPO as a feedstock for biofuel is met with resistance as its current price is becoming unattractive compared to soybean oil and gasoil. Palm oil is currently trading at a huge premium to gasoil of about US$197 per metric tonne, compared to an average discount of US$19 per metric tonne in the past year.
- The collapse in oil prices and the spread of Covid-19 have dragged down global markets. Indian oil companies announced a cut of Rs 2.69 per litre for petrol and Rs 2.33 per litre for diesel, marking the seventh consecutive daily reduction, driven by the coronavirus scare and Saudi Arabia's price cut in crude oil.

Market & Technicals:

Forward Views:

They are optimistic that CPO prices will recover due to the expectation of supply tightness for the eight vegetable oils in the first half of the year, but acknowledge that the continued presence of the Covid-19 outbreak, the oil price crisis, or continued weakness in market sentiment would likely put their 2020 CPO average selling price (ASP) forecast of RM2,500 per metric tonne at risk. - Jagran English reported that edible oil prices in India may come down by more than 10%, and wholesale prices (including palm oil) may fall by 10-15% in the next few months, providing significant relief to the central government.

Date/Timestamp: 2020-03-13
Value: CPO 540.86 USD/tonne; PKO 715.00 USD/tonne
Textual Content:
Supply:

The Central government permitted expansion in 18,100 hectares in new districts on a pilot basis. The grain export system has faced various challenges, including a one-week Canadian National Railway strike, heavy rain in Vancouver, a six-day outage of CN’s main southern line due to track washout, and track blockades, leading to a significant number of vessels waiting to be loaded at the West Coast (41 ships in Vancouver and 10 at Prince Rupert for week 30).

Demand:

- Malaysia is targeting North Africa and the Middle East as new export markets for its palm oil to reduce reliance on existing markets such as India, China, and the European Union. The Plantation Industries and Commodities Ministry has received calls from Middle Eastern ambassadors to discuss importing palm oil products and will undertake a comprehensive study via MPOB with the help of an international bank.
- Reduced demand from China, the epicenter of the Covid-19 virus, is a contributing factor to the decline in palm oil prices. China's soy oil stocks are 30% above the norm for this time of year due to stalled consumption as millions of people stayed home.

Policy & Trade:

India had previously curbed palm oil purchases from Malaysia in retaliation for comments by former Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad.

The most important thing is that we will continue to open up new markets, we will create a new direction."

Substitutes & Energy:

- Canola values have shown resilience in the face of drops in crude oil and broader markets. From January 1 to March 6, the May canola contract fell 6%, while May soybean oil in Chicago was down 19%, palm oil futures also fell about 19%, May soybeans 8%, corn 5.5%, and hard spring wheat 7.6%. Soybean meal, however, was down only about 1.4% (rallied after Argentina hiked its export tax).

- In India, soya refined oil was quoted at ₹785 for 10 kg, soya solvent at ₹735-40. Palm oil (Indore) ruled at ₹775, cotton oil (Gujarat) at ₹718, and cotton oil (Indore) at ₹770 for 10 kg. Groundnut oil was quoted higher at ₹1,230-1,250 for 10 kg.

Forward Views:

- Reuters quoted Indian traders saying it would take more than desire for detente for trade to resume between India and Malaysia, implying further actions might be needed beyond a desire for improved relations.

Deputy Minister Datuk Seri Dr Wee Jeck Seng will discuss with oil palm smallholders issues such as reintroducing subsidies, Malaysian Sustainable Palm Oil (MSPO) certification, foreign worker recruitment, and fresh fruit bunch (FFB) theft. Text-based negotiations for the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCEP) concluded in November 2019, aiming for economic integration of ASEAN with Australia, China, S. Korea, Japan, and New Zealand, with signing scheduled for late 2020.

Date/Timestamp: 2020-03-17
Value: CPO 527.02 USD/tonne; PKO 690.00 USD/tonne
Textual Content:

India's earlier advice to buyers to avoid Malaysian palm oil and restricted refined palm oil and palm olein imports significantly impacted demand.

Market participants note external macro factors like global equities and crude oil are driving the market more than fundamentals. Forward Views: AmInvestment Bank expects CB Industrial's plantation division in Central Kalimantan to remain in the red in FY20F due to high production costs and low CPO prices and production, and anticipates global discretionary demand for biodiesel to be weak due to low crude oil prices. A Malaysia-based producer had expected CPO prices to average MR 3,000/mt for Q1 and higher production in Malaysia from March onwards. Reuters technical analyst Wang Tao suggested palm oil may fall into a range of 2,100-2,184 ringgit per tonne.

Date/Timestamp: 2020-03-18
Value: CPO 521.34 USD/tonne; PKO 690.00 USD/tonne
Textual Content:
Supply: The Malaysian government's nationwide movement restriction order (March 18 for two weeks) initially raised fears for palm oil operations. However, the Cabinet later approved the plantation industry, including plantations and mills, to resume operations with immediate effect, provided precautionary measures against Covid-19 are taken. The Sarawak government had already granted an exemption for its oil palm industry. Before the Cabinet's approval, analysts, including CGS-CIMB's Ivy Ng, forecasted a potential loss of CPO supply of around 708,500 tonnes and a cut in end-March stockpile estimates to 1 million tonnes from 1.68 million tonnes due to the initial lockdown prospect. RHB Research indicated that unharvested FFB for two weeks would rot, leading to discounted prices and compromised oil quality, with a 2-3% impact on volume. Malaysia's February end-stocks fell to 1.68 million tonnes, the lowest since June 2017. FGV Holdings Bhd stated it would abide by all government regulations.
Demand: Malaysian palm oil exports for March 1-15 fell between 1.8% and 9.6% from the previous month. The real impact of a full shutdown on plantations would have been on exports, as Malaysian domestic consumption is 200,000-300,000 tonnes/month. India, a top vegetable oil importer, consumes about 1.9 million tonnes of edible oil a month, imports 1.25 million tonnes/month, and had less than a month's supply. China, the world's second-biggest edible oil importer, has declining soybean oil stockpiles. India's vegetable oil imports in February fell 11% y-o-y to 1.11 million tonnes, and overall imports for Nov-Feb decreased 6.1% to 4.56 million tonnes.
Policy & Trade: India dropped plans to lower import taxes on crude and refined vegetable oils (including palm oil, by 3-7%) due to shrinking government revenues, despite domestic prices rising over 11% after January's restrictions on Malaysian palm oil imports. India's finance ministry also shelved proposals to increase subsidized rice/wheat and provide vitamin-fortified rice. Indonesia will revoke rules requiring coal and palm oil exporters to use national shipping companies, as President Joko Widodo deemed them disruptive for exports. Malaysia's initial movement restriction order (March 18-31) aimed to curb coronavirus spread, with only CPO refining initially deemed essential. The Malaysian Palm Oil Association (MPOA) and Malayan Agricultural Producers Association (MAPA) appealed for broader exemptions, with MPOA initially stating their appeal was rejected before the Cabinet's subsequent approval.
Substitutes & Energy: Crude oil contracts on NYMEX fell due to the coronavirus economic impact and potential supply increase from Saudi Arabia and Russia, influencing CPO as a biodiesel ingredient. Soyoil prices on CBOT rose 2.28%, while Dalian's most-active soyoil contract gained 1.11% or fell 0.57%; Dalian palm oil contract gained 3.87% or dropped 0.17%.
Market & Technicals: Malaysian palm oil futures initially rose on Tuesday (benchmark June contract up 22 ringgit or 0.99% to 2,242 ringgit/$517.54) due to supply concerns from the lockdown, then jumped 5.42% on Wednesday (benchmark June contract up 122 ringgit to 2,372 ringgit/$544.91) before the exemption was officially announced. The ringgit fell 0.56% against the dollar, making palm oil cheaper. MCX CPO rose nearly 2% on subdued vegetable oil imports, while BMD key contracts capped upside, closing 0.4% lower (June contract at 2,240 ringgits). NCDEX soybean futures rose 1.6%. India's income tax revenues contracted 3.5% in the first 11 months of the fiscal year (April 2019 onwards), with other taxes growing 3.8%.
Forward Views: CGS-CIMB's Ivy Ng estimated a potential revenue loss of RM1.6 billion for the Malaysian palm oil industry if the RMO fully impacted operations. The reduced supply (if operations halted) would likely lead to CPO price increases, benefiting other producers like Indonesia and Thailand. Earnings of Malaysian-centric producers like FGV Holdings Bhd, Ta Ann Holdings Bhd, and IOI Corp Bhd would be hardest hit, while integrated players with Indonesian estates like Kuala Lumpur-Kepong Bhd (KLK) and Genting Plantations Bhd (GenP) would be partially cushioned. CGS-CIMB estimated potential negative earnings impacts of 30% for Hap Seng Plantations Bhd, 14% for Ta Ann, 6% for IOI, 4% for KLK, 7% for GENP, and 0.7% for Wilmar, and FGV possibly tilting into a RM3 million loss. CGS-CIMB is keeping its earnings forecasts and target prices pending further clarification. Reuters technical analyst Wang Tao suggested palm oil might test support at 2,184 ringgit per tonne, with a break potentially leading to a fall to 2,100 ringgit.

Date/Timestamp: 2020-03-19

The Malaysian Cabinet's decision to allow palm oil operations reversed an initial interpretation of the MCO, which had only deemed CPO refining as an essential service. Indonesia plans to revoke rules requiring coal and palm oil exporters to use national shipping companies, as President Joko Widodo deemed them disruptive for exports.

Date/Timestamp: 2020-03-23

Textual Content:
Supply:
*   Local plantation companies are implementing strict standard operating procedures (SOPs), including social distancing, for harvesting and milling operations to combat the COVID-19 outbreak and maintain production.
*   Malaysian Palm Oil Association (MPOA) CEO Datuk Mohamad Nageeb Ahmad Abdul Wahab confirmed comprehensive SOPs are in place, adhering to Health Ministry guidelines, with no reported COVID-19 cases at local estates so far.

*   The government lifted a control order on oil palm and rubber industries, allowing them to resume restricted operations from March 19. The oil palm sector anticipates a revenue loss of RM1.6 billion to RM1.8 billion if operations were to stop for two weeks.
*   The MPIC considers palm oil an essential item (cooking oil) and allows harvesting of fresh fruit bunches (FFB) by plantation companies and smallholders, processing of FFB by palm oil factories, and processing of crude palm oil (CPO) in refineries for domestic cooking oil production.
*   CGS-CIMB reported minimal impact on planters' earnings and industry revenue from the one-day closure of estates and mill operations.
*   Independent and organized smallholders own about 28.4% of Malaysia's 5.9 million hectares of planted oil palm estates. An MCO on the sector would significantly impact their daily income.

*   Integrated planters with majority-owned refineries and Indonesian estates (e.g., KLK, Genting Plantations Bhd, Wilmar Ltd) could be partially cushioned by better CPO prices from their Indonesian estates due to lower-than-expected Malaysian supply.
*   Malaysia's MCO from March 18 until end of March affects palm oil plantation activities, with supply predicted to fall by 350,000-700,000 metric tons in March. Reuters reported on March 18 that the Malaysian government would instruct plantations to resume operations.
*   Indonesia's output is expected to expand marginally this year, while Malaysia faces de-growth.

Date/Timestamp: 2020-06-22

Textual Content:
Supply:
- Malaysia is facing an acute labor shortage in the plantation sector, exacerbated by the COVID-19 pandemic and border closures, which could "potentially cripple" operations if foreign worker entry continues to be disallowed. United Plantations (UP) fears a surge in outflow of foreign workers when borders reopen.
- Malaysia's plantation and commodity sectors currently have 220,000 local and 265,397 foreign workers but still require 500,000 workers.
- The industry has reduced labor dependency by 30% over 10 years (from one employee per seven hectares to one per nine hectares) and aims for a 40% reduction (one employee per 10 hectares) through mechanization.
- PT Astra Agro Lestari reported a 8.5% year-on-year (YoY) fall in fresh fruit bunches (FFB) production to 1.1 million tons and a 14.6% YoY fall in Crude Palm Oil (CPO) production to 354 tons in Q1 2020.
- For independent farmers in Indonesia, FFB prices fell to less than Rp 1,000 (0.71 US cents) per kilogram, while partnered farmers saw prices between Rp 1,200 and Rp 1,300 per kilogram. A price below Rp 1,100 per kg is difficult for farmers.
- FGV Holdings expects to raise FFB production in FY20 due to a higher percentage of young and prime trees (old trees reduced from 49% in 2012 to 30%).
- FGV's Q1 2020 FFB production fell 33% to 712,000 tonnes from 1.06 million tonnes last year, impacting CPO deliveries which reduced by 33% to 514,000 tonnes from 762,000 tonnes.
- Rising production data from the Malaysian Palm Oil Association (MPOA) and Southern Peninsular Palm Oil Millers Association (SPPOMA) may weigh on prices.
Demand:
- India and China are starting to replenish palm oil stocks. India is expected to import 9-9.5 million tonnes this year, and China 6-6.5 million tonnes.
- In Q1 2020, India imported 1 million tonnes less palm oil, and China 700,000 tonnes less compared to the same period last year, according to Oil World.
- Last year, India consumed a record 10.3 million tonnes, and China 7 million tonnes. Palm oil constitutes 55-58% of China's annual 25% vegetable oils and fats imports.
- Demand for vegetable oils destined for the energy sector (biodiesel) is an important determinant of palm oil prices.
- Global fuel demand is recovering, but a record jump in global coronavirus cases could curb recovery.
Policy & Trade:
- India is scrutinizing trade arrangements, including SAFTA, ASEAN, and bilateral pacts, to reduce import dependence on China and plug loopholes that aid Chinese imports, citing suspicion of circumvention of FTAs and violations of rules of origin.
- The Indonesian government is injecting Rp2.78 trillion into the Oil Palm Plantation Fund Management Agency (BPDPKS) for the B30 project, to cover deficits of FAME producers due to falling diesel prices. The BPDPKS had previously subsidized the B30 program by Rp21.7 trillion from 2015-2017.
- The BPDPKS has not received income for almost half a year because CPO prices fell below the export levy threshold (US$50/ton). The Corruption Eradication Commission stated in 2016 there was no legal basis for using plantation funds for subsidies.
- Indonesia's government reduced the BBN production target from 9.59 million kiloliters to 7.83 million kiloliters due to COVID-19 impact on fuel consumption.
- West Sumatera in Indonesia has officially imposed province-wide large-scale social restrictions (PSBB).

- Asian buyers are increasingly turning to U.S. crude oil (like WTI Midland and Eagle Ford) for cheaper supply due to OPEC+ output cuts, sharp swings in official selling prices from Saudi Arabia and Iraq, and lower freight rates across the Pacific. WTI Midland spot premium rose $2/barrel, while Murban rose $4/barrel. The cost of hiring a Very Large Crude Carrier from the U.S. Gulf Coast to China was around $7.5 million in mid-June, down from $15 million in late April.

- The benchmark September 2020 CPO futures closed at RM2,475 a tonne on Friday, the highest in four months.
- Weekly turnover on Bursa Malaysia Derivatives shed to 256,328 lots from 245,808 lots, while open interest decreased to 227,871 contracts from 252,401 contracts.

Forward Views:

- United Plantations (UP) CEO Datuk Carl Bek-Nielsen believes much of the bearish expectations for palm oil prices have already been priced into the market.
- FGV chairman Datuk Wira Azhar Abdul Hamid expects CPO prices to range between RM2,200 and RM2,400 for 2020 and anticipates a "slight dip" in FGV's financial performance this year despite higher Q2 FFB production.
- Palm oil trader David Ng expects CPO futures to trade higher next week, driven by increased export data, stronger Dalian Commodity Exchange performance, and sustained Brent crude oil prices, which should lower Malaysian stock levels.
- Malacca Securities expects "choppiness" in the market but believes firmer crude oil and CPO prices may provide a cushion for volatility. They project FBM KLCI to recover towards 1,550 if the 1,500 psychological level holds.
- Market players project the Jakarta Composite Index (JCI) to end the year between 5,000 and 5,500 due to pandemic-related volatility.
- Schroders Indonesia investment director Irwanti expects JCI to drop 15% in a best-case scenario.
- Mandiri Sekuritas head of equity research Adrian Joezer forecasts a 12% JCI drop to 5,540 by year-end, contingent on market response to government policies and COVID-19 developments.
- Batavia Prosperindo Aset Manajemen (BPAM) projects JCI to close the year between 5,000 and 5,300 (a 15-20% fall from last year's end point of 6,299).
- Eastspring Investments Indonesia chief investment officer Ari Pitojo noted market consensus for a rebound to normal levels in 1.5 to 2 years.
- Mirae Asset Sekuritas head of research Hariyanto Wijaya projects JCI to reach 5,180 by end-2020 in a best-case scenario or 5,830 if mass vaccines are produced and CPO prices rise. His bear-case scenario is 4,160 if a second wave occurs, the US enters recession, and CPO prices collapse.
- The Indonesian government projected a baseline economic growth of 2.3% this year and a 0.4% contraction under a worst-case scenario.
- The Malaysian Palm Oil Council’s (MPOC) ‘Pointers on Price Trends’ online event (June 22-28) is being watched for price and production outlook.

Textual Content:
Supply:
- Three oil palm processing plants had their licenses withdrawn by Malaysia's Environment Department (DoE) for contaminating water supply. These were among 330 factories nationwide that faced enforcement actions (compounds, suspended licenses, seized equipment) for violating the Environmental Quality Act 1974 during the Movement Control Order (MCO) from March 18 to June 22.
- Industry expert Dr James Fry from LMC International Ltd predicts Malaysian palm oil stocks could surge as much as 50% to 3 million tonnes by year-end, with little impact of coronavirus on production. The Malaysian Palm Oil Board (MPOB) estimated 2020 closing stocks to rise 14.4% to 2.3 million tonnes.
- The Malaysian government's ban on foreign labor recruitment until year-end is expected to significantly impact the labor-intensive plantation sector, where foreign labor constitutes 84.1% of the workforce, with 38% as harvesters/collectors and 33% as field workers.
- The Malaysian Palm Oil Association (MPOA) stated that Malaysia loses 10-20% of potential production annually due to worker shortages, a problem exacerbated by the pandemic. Thousands of foreign workers, including from Indonesia, left during the MCO, with fears of further departures when borders fully reopen. This could delay harvesting and reduce oil output.
- MPOB forecasts Malaysia's 2020 crude palm oil output to fall 4.3% to 19 million tonnes.
- Malaysian palm oil producers like FGV Holdings and IOI Corp Bhd are implementing retention initiatives, including contract renewals, new facilities (e.g., e-wallet, sundry shops), corporate social responsibility programs, and extra cash for workers extending contracts beyond two years, adding to the 30-40% labor cost share.
- Wilmar International is intensifying local recruitment and boosting productivity with training. MPOA advocates for government-issued foreign work permits for harvesters.
Demand:
- Traders fear that the surge in demand and exports would lose steam if a second wave of COVID-19 occurs.
- Malaysian palm oil exports for June 1-20 rose between 55.3% and 57% according to cargo surveyors, driven by easing coronavirus curbs and an export duty exemption. However, follow-up buying from destination markets like China, Pakistan, Bangladesh, and Europe is needed to sustain these exceptionally strong exports, according to Anilkumar Bagani of Sunvin Group.
- The Malaysian Palm Oil Council (MPOC) stated that exports are likely to increase further in the second half of the year.
- EU palm oil imports in the 2019/20 season (since July) were down 11% at 5.55 million tonnes by June 21, according to official EU data.
- Leading analyst Thomas Mielke (Oil World) stated that global consumption of palm oil will fall this season for the first time on record (by 2.2 million tonnes, or about 3%, from last season) due to a coronavirus-led recession. He expects overall demand this year to remain poor, picking up next season, as the lingering effect of COVID-19 will curtail disposable income, especially for food in developing countries.
- James Fry (LMC International) noted that food demand has been damaged, highlighting the hospitality sector (fast food, snack bars, hotels) as significant palm oil consumers that have been severely hit by the pandemic.
- China, according to Cai Neng Bin of Shanghai Pansun, may not have a strong intention to replenish its current low palm oil stocks given increasing CPO prices.
- Abah Ofon of 3XG UK Consulting Limited expects Malaysian CPO exports to Africa to increase to about 9 million tonnes this year (compared to 6 million tonnes over the last decade), with Africa accounting for 12-13% of global CPO consumption but only 4% of global output. Kenya, Tanzania, Ghana, Ethiopia, and Djibouti are growing markets.
- Emily French of ConsiliAgra expects food demand to recover in India, China, and Pakistan, which would benefit palm oil.
- Indonesia is seeing increased exports of palm oil-derived oleochemical products such as soap glycerine noodles, fatty acids, and chemical ingredients due to COVID-19, and domestic demand for soap and daily food products is increasing. However, demand for frying oil and food solids is lower due to slowing consumer demand.
- U.R. Unnithan of Sumwin Group projects bearish gross domestic diesel demand for 2020, declining 3%, then increasing to 4.5% in 2021.     *   The Malaysian Palm Oil Board (MPOB) announced it will introduce seven new commercialized technologies for the upstream and downstream sectors at its Transfer of Technology (TOT) virtual seminar on July 7, aimed at improving yield, production efficiency, avoiding wastage, and developing higher-value products like margarine, cosmetics, and palm milk. MPOB has developed 667 technologies, with 30% commercialized, holding a market value of RM3.5 billion.
    *   The Malaysian Palm Oil Association (MPOA) anticipated lower palm oil production in May compared to April, primarily due to labor shortages caused by the lockdown measures.
    *   The impact of dry weather and reduced fertilizer application by farmers last year is expected to continue affecting palm fruit production in 2020, potentially leading to a correction in seasonal harvests during the second half of the year (which accounts for 60% of annual production).
    *   PT Asian Agri Director Fadhil Hasan reiterated that Indonesian crude palm oil production might decrease by 1-2 million tons from last year's 44 million tons.
    *   MPOB projected Malaysian output could fall 4.3% to 19 million tons due to biological stress on trees and limited labor supply.
    *   Joko Supriyono, Chairman of the Indonesian Palm Oil Association, emphasized that the pandemic is a catalyst for the industry to adopt more efficient operations due to its labor-intensive nature, as good margins cannot be taken for granted.
*   **Demand**
    *   Demand for edible oils from hotels, restaurants, and the catering (HoReCa) sector in India has increased following the relaxation of lockdown curbs, leading to higher prices for refined soyoil and crude palm oil futures on NCDEX and MCX.
    *   Trading activities are expected to pick up in India in the coming weeks and months as lockdown phases gradually end. Exports are anticipated to recover, supported by a firm USD against the Rupee.
    *   Indian importers have resumed purchases of Malaysian palm oil, with large importers finalizing contracts for 200,000 tonnes of crude palm oil from Malaysia during the first fortnight of May.
    *   Sathia Varqa, owner of Palm Oil Analytics, predicted that edible oil consumption will return, and oleochemicals demand will rise due to their use in personal hygiene products. He noted that Malaysia is positioned to benefit from the reopening of India and China, offering relatively lower prices than Indonesia and experiencing warming trade relations with India.
*   **Policy & Trade**
    *   Malaysia is initiating legal action against the European Union (EU) through a World Trade Organization (WTO) dispute settlement mechanism, citing allegedly discriminatory "anti-palm oil campaign" policies. Plantation Industries and Commodities Minister Datuk Dr Mohd Khairuddin Aman Razali stated that the EU's Renewable Energy Directive II (EU RED II) Delegation Regulation unjustly categorizes palm oil as having a high indirect land use change (ILUC) rate, restricting free trade and negatively impacting over 3 million Malaysians in the palm oil industry and more than 500,000 smallholders. Malaysia will also join Indonesia as a third party in its WTO case against the EU.
    *   The Indonesian government is allocating $195 million (2.78 trillion rupiah) from the state budget to subsidize palm oil biodiesel producers, as confirmed by Mongabay.com. This decision has drawn criticism from campaigners and small oil palm farmer associations, who argue that the state palm oil fund (BPDP-KS) is intended to empower small farmers, not subsidize large multinational corporations like Wilmar International, which has historically been a major beneficiary of these subsidies. Small farmers are currently struggling with low CPO prices, such as 700 rupiah/kg in Jambi province, down from 1,200 rupiah/kg. The Finance Minister indicated a total of $250 million is needed for the biodiesel program, with the balance potentially coming from increased export tariffs. Critics question the use of state budget funds for biodiesel subsidies and the transparency of BPDP-KS fund distribution. Greenpeace Indonesia also raised concerns about the environmental impact of palm oil production and companies failing to pay fines for land and forest fires.
    *   Indonesia's reference price for Crude Palm Oil (CPO) for July 2020 export duty (Bea Keluar/BK) is set at US$622.47/ton, an increase of US$53.53 (9.41%) from June 2020's US$568.94/ton. The government maintains a zero export duty (US$0/ton) for CPO in July because the reference price remains below the US$750/ton threshold.
    *   PT Daimler Commercial Vehicles Indonesia (DCVI) and Tri Yuswidjajanto Zaenuri (ITB Energy Conversion Expert) advised diesel vehicle users of B30 (30% CPO content) to regularly monitor fuel filters and water separators and clean fuel tanks every six months.
    *   Howie Lee, an economist at Oversea-Chinese Banking Corp., expressed concerns about Indonesia's commitment to maintaining its B30 biofuel mandate. The Indonesian trade ministry has revised its biofuel consumption forecast to approximately 8 million kiloliters this year, a reduction from the initial target of 9.6 million kiloliters. Malaysia has also postponed its B20 mandate in certain areas due to pandemic-related infrastructure delays.
*   **Substitutes & Energy**
    *   Malaysian palm oil futures rose due to stronger crude prices and costlier rival oils.
    *   Crude oil prices rose following a sharp drop in U.S. oil stockpiles, making palm oil a more attractive option for biodiesel feedstock. However, gains were capped by worries over a halt in fuel demand recovery, as the United States recorded its biggest one-day spike in COVID-19 cases, and California reimposed some lockdown measures.
    *   Palm oil's rival soyoil rallied to a near three-month high overnight on the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) due to concerns that hot and dry weather could stress crops and reduce yield potential (up 0.4% in early trade, 0.5% by close). Dalian's most-active soyoil contract rose 1.7% in early trade and 1.8% by close, while its palm oil contract fell 0.4% in early trade and rose 1.3% by close.
    *   Chicago corn futures fell for the first time in five sessions after climbing to their highest since late-March, as the market took a breather following lower U.S. planting figures.
    *   The overall trend for the oil complex sector looks positive due to strong fundamentals. Refined soybean oil is expected to show a firm trend this week, though with capped upside, supported by strong global cues and improved import prospects for Malaysian palm oil in India.
    *   The USD's firmness against the Rupee could further support export prices. Lowering trade war issues between the US and China are seen as a supportive factor moving forward.
    *   Speculators on CBOT increased long positions in soybean futures and options to 44,285 contracts by June 23 (from 21,183 a week earlier), anticipating a recovery in US trade with China.
*   **Market & Technicals**
    *   Malaysian palm oil futures rose for a second straight session on Thursday (July 2). The benchmark September delivery contract on the BMD rose 0.3% to 2,333 ringgit ($544.71) a tonne in early trade and closed 1.5% higher at 2,361 ringgit ($551.25).
    *   Reuters analyst Wang Tao suggested palm oil might retest a resistance at 2,351 ringgit per tonne.
    *   On the Multi Commodity Exchange (MCX) in India, the July crude palm oil contract was up 0.7% at 664.8 rupees per 10 kg. Weakness in BMD crude palm oil contracts due to global demand outlook amid COVID-19 restricted significant rises on MCX.
    *   On the National Commodity and Derivatives Exchange (NCDEX) in India, the July soybean contract was up 0.3% at 3,766.0 rupees per 100 kg, hitting a nearly one-week high of 3,790 rupees per 100 kg due to improved demand from crushing plants. However, this was limited by tepid soymeal demand from exporters.
    *   The NCDEX July refined soyoil contract was up 0.02% at 809.3 rupees per 10 kg, and the July mustard contract was up 0.2% at 4,701.0 rupees per 100 kg, supported by government procurement from farmers at minimum support prices.
*   **Forward Views**
    *   The Malaysian Palm Oil Council (MPOC) anticipated CPO prices could reach MYR2,594 per ton (US$605 per ton) in H2 2020, with an average of MYR2,337 by year-end, provided Indonesia and Malaysia continue their biodiesel mandates and European vegetable oil production declines, encouraging buyers to switch to palm oil.
    *   Veteran analyst Dorab Mistry maintained that 2020 has been a "cruel season" for palm oil, with prices down 23% year-to-date compared to soybean oil's 18% decline. Concerns regarding new waves of virus infections, extended lockdowns, and renewed trade friction between the U.S. and China may cloud the palm oil outlook.
    *   James Fry, chairman of LMC International, stated that the global market continues to face a supply glut that could reach "well above" 3 million tons by the end of the year.
    *   Religare Broking analysts projected that the July refined soyoil contract on NCDEX is likely to touch Rs 820-825 per 10 kg, and the July soybean contract is likely to reach Rs 3,850 per quintal by the end of this week. They maintain a bullish long-term outlook for the agri sector despite short-term profit booking and good monsoon reports.

Analysis from Invezz highlighted the ongoing El Nino event as a factor complicating supply dynamics, with some parts of Indonesia experiencing very dry weather, water shortages, and crop failures, expected to lower supplies. Higher demand is also expected from ASEAN and Middle East & North Africa regions due to inadequate domestic production and competitive palm oil prices. Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) shows significant growth potential, having imported 3.5 million tonnes in 2022, with per capita consumption expected to rise with improving economic conditions. India aims to increase its domestic palm oil supplies from 270,000 tonnes in 2019-2020 to 1.12 million tons by 2025 as part of its self-sufficiency goal. Malaysian palm oil exports for July rose 7.8% (AmSpec Agri Malaysia) and 14% (Intertek Testing Services - ITS) from the previous month.

This initiative is part of Indonesia's efforts to expand the use of palm oil in fuels to reduce expensive fossil fuel imports, having already rolled out B35 (35% palm oil blend) this year. Engine tests will be followed by ground and flight tests later in August.

Stronger crude oil futures make palm a more attractive option for biodiesel feedstock.

However, the contract was unable to make a significant recovery from a 3.02% drop on the preceding Monday. Trading was described as directionless due to a lack of fresh positive data and cautious sentiment ahead of July supply and demand estimates. Earlier, on Monday (July 31st), Malaysian palm oil futures had fallen for a fifth consecutive session, with the October contract shedding 2.07% to 3,923 ringgit per tonne in early trade, reaching its weakest in nearly two weeks, although it had risen 3.43% so far for the month of July.

The funds are earmarked for constructing a biodiesel plant and a palm oil refinery at Owendo port, a fourth plant in Mouila, a crude palm oil processing plant in Lambaréné, and maintaining existing facilities, including 63,330 hectares of palm oil plantations, three palm oil mills, kernel crushing plants, a CPO refinery, and the Awala biogas cogeneration plant. However, experts like Professor William Laurance (James Cook University) and Kiki Taufik (Greenpeace) dismissed these claims as "goofy" and "criminally misleading," citing scientific evidence that tropical rainforests store significantly more carbon (exceeding 400 metric tonnes per hectare) than mature oil palm plantations (typically between 2-10 times less). The decline, which marked the seventh fall in eight sessions, was attributed to losses in rival edible oils and concerns over lacklustre demand. *   The Malaysian Palm Oil Board (MPOB) signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with the Indian Vegetable Oil Producers’ Association (IVPA) on August 4 in New Delhi. The MoU aims to promote collaboration in sustainable vegetable oil production and trade, technology transfer, capacity building in palm-oil based industries, and best practices. MPOB Director-General Datuk Dr Ahmad Parveez Ghulam Kadir stated it would encourage commercial and technical exchange. IVPA President Sudhakar Desai noted India can benefit from Malaysia's advanced knowledge. India is Malaysia's top palm oil export destination, purchasing 1.22 million tonnes in the first six months of 2023, representing 17.3% of Malaysia’s export volume for the period.
*   Malaysia's Plantation and Commodities Ministry (KPK), led by Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof, will propose oil palm replanting grants to the Finance Ministry for the next budget. Currently, the government provides soft loans through Agrobank for replanting, fertilizers, pesticides, agricultural inputs, and tools, with a 2% interest/management fee and repayment starting in the fifth year.
*   Malaysia and Indonesia, the world's largest palm oil producers, agreed to establish an ad hoc joint task force (JTF) with the European Union (EU) to build mutual understanding on the EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR) implementation and its core aspects, including benchmarking. The first meeting of the JTF was held on August 4 in Jakarta, co-chaired by Indonesia’s Food and Agribusiness Deputy Minister Musdhalifah Machmud, Malaysia’s Plantation and Commodities Ministry secretary-general Datuk Mad Zaidi Mohd Karli, and European Commission Green Diplomacy and Multilateralism director Astrid Schomaker. The Council of Palm Oil Producing Countries (CPOPC) facilitated the meeting. The JTF aims to address concerns raised by Indonesia and Malaysia regarding EUDR implementation and identify practical solutions. Key issues for the JTF include smallholders in the supply chain, national certification schemes (land legality and cut-off date for deforestation), producer-to-end-consumer traceability, scientific data on deforestation and forest degradation, and data protection. The JTF is scheduled to conclude its work by end-2024, with a possible extension, and its next meeting is tentatively scheduled for end-November 2023.

Supply:

The stockpile stood at 2.31 million tonnes. This production level was the highest over the past two years, surpassing the previous peak of 1.81 million tonnes in October 2022.

They expect palm oil stocks to still exceed two million tonnes potentially until the end of the year, at least. The stock/usage (S/U) ratio is now at 12%, which is above the 15-year historical average of 10%.

- Hong Leong Investment Bank (HLIB) Research expects palm oil stockpile to likely remain flattish in October, as a seasonally higher cropping pattern will likely be offset by potentially stronger near-term demand for palm oil.

They think Malaysian palm oil stocks will continue to recover to pre-pandemic levels as labour scarcity has steadily decreased.
