Groundbreaking is planned for early next year, with commercial operations expected in 2Q25. The facility will have the capacity to produce 500,000 tons of biofeedstock and edible oil annually. The joint venture, ARC, will also jointly pursue the business of collecting waste materials generated from the palm oil refining facility.

Factors such as harvest timing, processing temperature, and water sources can affect the levels of these substances. The edible oil industry needs to work on removing such elements to maintain consumer trust.

Year-to-date palm oil closing stocks in major importing countries have reached pre-pandemic levels: India (4.2 million tonnes), China (5.7 million tonnes), Pakistan (2.7 million tonnes), and Bangladesh (1 million tonnes). MIDF anticipates demand would be sluggish in the remainder of the second half (2H2023).

India usually imports around 200,000 tonnes of sunflower oil per month but has recently made purchases of more than 300,000 tonnes.

POSCO International hopes to expand its palm oil business value chain, while GS Caltex expects to enhance its biofuel production technology and secure a stable procurement of biofuel feedstock through recycling waste palm oil.

- The European Food Safety Authority recently noted that 3-MCPD is considered safe for most consumers.
- Winterisation, a method that makes palm oil healthier by reducing total saturated fatty acids, could be applied without harming its use in medicine.

The country expects its futures-based CPO reference price to be ready by Q1 2024, intending to no longer rely on Malaysian and Rotterdam CPO prices. Trading on Indonesia's newly launched CPO futures exchange is scheduled to begin on October 23, with 18 businesses ready to participate voluntarily. Nigeria's Central Bank fully liberalized the country's foreign exchange market by lifting the dollar ban on 43 items, including palm oil.

Crude oil prices hovered above $90 a barrel; weaker crude oil typically makes palm oil a less attractive option for biodiesel feedstock.

The Malaysian Ringgit (MYR=) fell by 0.32% against the dollar, making the commodity cheaper for buyers holding foreign currency. Textual Content:
Supply: Datuk Seri Mohd Shafie Apdal stated that at least 20% of oil palm in Malaysia remains unharvested due to labor shortages, calling for additional government initiatives to address this. Data from the Southern Peninsular Palm Oil Millers Association (SPPOMA), as noted by LSEG Agriculture Research, showed that production in the first half of October fell by 0.73% month-on-month. In Indonesia, the Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources (ESDM) advocated for increased use of empty oil palm fruit bunches (EOPFBs) as biomass raw materials for co-firing in coal-fired power plants (PLTU). PLN Energi Primer Indonesia (PLN EPI) committed to supporting a national co-firing utilization target of 10.2 million tons by 2025 and engaged in a collaboration with PT Elektrika Construction Nusantara (EKN) to use EOPFB waste at the Bengkayang PLTU in West Kalimantan, absorbing 40 local workers. Demand: Malaysian palm oil product exports for October 1-15 rose by 5.6% (AmSpec Agri Malaysia) and 7.3% (Intertek Testing Services) compared to September 1-15, indicating strong demand. The federal government in Pakistan reduced the prices of popular ghee and cooking oil brands at Utility Stores by up to Rs38 per kilogram and Rs36 per liter, respectively, to improve financial ease for consumers.
Policy & Trade: Malaysia maintained its November crude palm oil export duty at 8%. The reference price for November was set lower at 3,556.08 ringgit (US$751.81) per metric ton, down from October's reference price of 3,710.50 ringgit/ton. The export tax structure ranges from 3% for CPO between RM2,250 and RM2,400 per ton, up to a maximum of 8% when prices exceed RM3,450 per ton. Datuk Seri Mohd Shafie Apdal urged a review of the taxes imposed on the palm oil industry, which include a 24% income tax rate, a 3% windfall tax, a 7.5% service tax (SST) for companies in Sabah and 5.0% for Sarawak, a RM16 per tonne levy on crude palm oil production, and a RM2,200 per person levy extension charge by the Immigration Department for workers employed for over 10 years.
Substitutes & Energy: Chicago soyoil prices were weaker. Crude oil prices stabilized after a decline on Monday, influenced by hopes of easing U.S. sanctions on Venezuela and efforts to prevent an escalation of the conflict in Gaza. Weaker crude oil prices make palm oil less appealing as a feedstock for biodiesel.

Date/Timestamp: 2023-10-19
Value: CPO 786.43 USD/tonne; PKO 920.00 USD/tonne
Textual Content:
Supply: The US soybean oil stocks held by National Oilseed Processors Association (Nopa) members totaled 1.108 billion pounds as of September 30, the lowest since December 2014 and 24% below year-ago levels. These stocks represented 14.7 days of use, the lowest in over a decade. The US Department of Agriculture (USDA) projects total domestic soybean oil use at a record 27.45 billion pounds in 2023-24 and expects US soyoil ending stocks to be at a seven-year low with the lightest stocks-to-use in a decade. Despite a disappointing soybean crop, the USDA forecasts record US soybean processing in 2023-24. India's Union government plans to establish palm oil plantations over 840,344 hectares (8403.44 sqkm) in six northeastern states (Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Manipur, Mizoram, Nagaland, and Tripura) as part of the National Mission on Edible Oils (Palm Oil) (NMEO-OP) launched in 2021-22, aiming to boost edible oil and CPO production and reduce import reliance.
Demand: US soybean oil exports are anticipated to reach all-time lows in 2023-24, accounting for approximately 1% of global trade. In 2022-23, the US became a net importer of soybean oil for the first time. To meet domestic biofuel demand, US canola oil imports surged by 38% to a record 2.8 million tonnes in 2022-23, and imports of animal and vegetable fats and oils (including used cooking oil) increased by almost 240% to 882,000 tonnes during the first 11 months of 2022-23, with China being the largest supplier at 37%. Musim Mas, a Singapore-based Indonesian palm oil exporter controlling 18% of the global refined and processed palm oil market, has halted exports of palm oil from independent small farmers to the EU due to the new EU deforestation regulation. It now directs palm oil from small farmers to the Asia-Pacific market, which contributed over 60% of the company's $10.8 billion revenue in 2022, while sourcing from its own operations and corporate suppliers with corporate traceability statistics for EU markets. Major importer China's active purchasing for reserve restocking contributed to price increases, according to Mitesh Saiya of Kantilal Laxmichand & Company Mumbai.
Policy & Trade: The European Union's new deforestation regulation (EUDR) is described as a "big challenge" and "trade barrier" for palm oil exporters like Musim Mas, requiring importers to provide a due diligence statement by late 2024 (mid-2025 for micro and small enterprises) to prove products do not originate from deforested land. Musim Mas has adjusted its supply chain to comply, no longer exporting palm oil from Indonesian small farmers to the EU.
Substitutes & Energy: The most actively traded Chicago soybean oil futures are at three-year lows for the date, having declined by 20% from a year ago and more than 15% over the last two months. Biomass-based (D4) credits, for which soybean oil is the primary feedstock for US biofuel and renewable diesel production, reached three-year lows last week, falling by as much as 45% since early September. Dalian's most-active soyoil contract rose 0.3%, while its palm oil contract declined 0.1%. Soyoil prices on the Chicago Board of Trade fell 0.3%.
Market & Technicals: Malaysian palm oil futures for January delivery closed up 1 ringgit (0.03%) at 3,781 ringgit ($798.69) on Tuesday, hovering at a near three-week high.
Forward Views: The USDA anticipates that the increasing trend of alternative vegetable oil imports will continue over the next year, maintaining competition with domestic soybean oil.

Value: CPO 785.34 USD/tonne; PKO 920.00 USD/tonne
Textual Content:
Demand: Malaysia's total exports in September decreased by 13.7% year-on-year to 124.47 billion ringgit (approximately US$26.14 billion), largely due to weaker global demand, uncertainties in commodity prices, and a high base effect from the previous year. Exports of agricultural goods, which constitute 6.5% of total exports, fell by 23.1%, primarily driven by lower exports and weaker prices of palm oil and palm oil-based products. Imports declined by 11.1% to 99.95 billion ringgit. Consequently, Malaysia's total trade for September was down 12.6% to 224.43 billion ringgit, with the trade surplus contracting by 23% to 24.52 billion ringgit. For Q3 2023, Malaysia's total trade decreased by 15.7% to 653.57 billion ringgit. In 2022, Russia imported palm oil from Malaysia as part of a bilateral trade turnover that reached US$2.66 billion in 2021 (up 23.8%) and grew by another 12.1% in 2022, with agricultural product and food trade increasing by 18% in 2022. However, Russia was not among Malaysia's top 30 export partners in Q1 2023.
Policy & Trade: Indonesia stated its readiness to collaborate with Malaysia to oppose the European Union Deforestation Regulation (EUDR), viewing it as discriminatory and an impediment to CPO sales in EU countries. The Head of the Commodities Futures Trading Regulatory Agency (Bappebti), Didid Noordiatomoko, confirmed ongoing discussions regarding the form of this collaboration, emphasizing cooperation over competition between the two CPO-producing nations, both of which have established CPO exchanges. Malaysia's Plantation and Commodities Ministry (KPK) received an increased allocation of RM732.7 million in the 2024 Budget, based on industry feedback. This funding will focus on new economic initiatives, biomass utilization (using recyclable wastes to generate revenue), achieving higher and more efficient production through technology and innovation, and expanding market access for downstream products globally. Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof confirmed the RM100 million allocation for the Palm Replanting Programme Incentive for smallholders. The second meeting of the Ad Hoc Joint Task Force (JTF) is scheduled for December in Malaysia, where Malaysia hopes EU representatives will consider palm oil producers' perspectives during the implementation of EUDR-related rules. Russia and Malaysia are also working to finalize a new Double Tax Agreement (DTA) to simplify tax regimes for businesses and are increasingly using non-dollar currencies, such as Chinese yuan and dirhams, for payments.

Date/Timestamp: 2023-10-23
Value: CPO 780.33 USD/tonne; PKO 910.00 USD/tonne
Textual Content:
Supply: Nigeria's palm oil output is estimated at 900,000-1.3 million metric tonnes (MT), with the industry fragmented and 80% dominated by small-scale farmers lacking access to improved seedlings and modern practices, leading to lower yields. The Nigerian Institute for Oil Palm Research (NIFOR) will establish a permanent base in Cross River State, Nigeria, for training and capacity building. Market players are awaiting palm oil production data from the Southern Peninsula Palm Oil Millers’ Association and Malaysian Palm Oil Association.
Demand: Malaysian palm oil product exports for Oct 1-20 rose 7.9% to 885,888 tonnes from 821,408 tonnes shipped from Sept 1-20, according to AmSpec Agri Malaysia, or between 7.9% and 9.9% according to Intertek Testing Services. Nigeria’s palm oil imports from Malaysia increased by 65.3% in the first nine months of 2023, rising to 234,324 MT from 141,786 MT in the corresponding period of 2022, an increase of 92,538 MT, based on Malaysian Palm Oil Council data. Nigeria faces a national demand of 2.1 million MT and a supply gap of around 800,000 MT, with annual imports estimated at over N500 billion. India and China showed persistent buying interest. Pakistan, a major importer of palm oil from Indonesia, consumes around 4.5 million tons of edible oil annually.

Indonesia's Crude Palm Oil (CPO) exchange (Indonesia Commodity and Derivatives Exchange - ICDX) began its first physical CPO spot trading on Friday (October 20 or 21), with four lots of 25 MT of CPO trading at 11,305 rupiah ($0.7130) per kg for 15-day delivery to Dumai. 18 companies were expected to participate initially. Trade through the exchange is currently voluntary.

Dalian's most-active soyoil contract fell 1.36%, while its palm oil contract was down 1.82%. Soyoil prices on the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) were up 0.76%.

Forward Views: Palm oil trader David Ng expects next week’s price to trade between RM3,650 and RM3,900 per tonne, anticipating positive momentum to sustain due to better demand, increased exports, and a weaker ringgit. Reuters technical analyst Wang Tao stated palm oil may retrace further to 3,682 ringgit per metric ton.

Textual Content:
Supply: The cost of replanting oil palm stands at RM20,000 to RM25,000 per hectare, meaning the government's RM100 million allocation for replanting incentives would only be sufficient for replanting 4,000 hectares. Brazil still has available stocks from its record crop, with shipments poised to beat estimates, but a historic drought in Brazil’s Amazon is disrupting river transport and forcing some soy and corn shipments to be rerouted. The Mississippi River, which funnels US soybeans to Gulf Coast ports, has shriveled due to drought.
Demand: Robust Malaysian palm oil export performance for Oct 1-20 (estimated up 7.9% to 9.9% by AmSpec Agri and Intertek Testing Services) and stronger Indian palm oil purchases limited the decline in prices. US soybean export sales are down 40% from a year earlier. China, the largest soybean importer, booked at least 95 cargoes from Brazil for delivery until the end of November, with 52 vessels scheduled for next month compared to seven for the same week last year. China’s imports of soybeans from Brazil rose 23% in September. China’s soybean purchases are down by 200 million bushels year-on-year, accounting for two-thirds of the overall drop in US soybean exports. The USDA's current export projection for US soybeans is 1.755 billion bushels, down 70 million bushels from a couple of months ago, 237 million from last year, and 511 million from 2020, representing a roughly 22% pullback in exports over 3 years. Soybean processing margins have rebounded since June due to a poor harvest in Argentina boosting demand for American crops, along with increased demand from the renewable-diesel industry and a bumper crop in Brazil. Louis Dreyfus Co. is building a soybean processing plant in Ohio with an annual capacity of 1.5 million metric tons, to boost vegetable oil production for cooking and fuel.
Policy & Trade: Jelebu MP Datuk Seri Jalaluddin Alias urged palm oil and palm-based product exporters, whose total export earnings reached RM137.89 billion in 2022 (RM19.77 billion from 3.78 million tonnes of palm oil and RM118.12 billion from 22.75 million tonnes of palm-based products), to contribute 0.001% (RM137 million) to the oil palm replanting fund. The Prime Minister announced RM100 million in incentives (grants and loans) for the oil palm replanting program to 7,000 private smallholders in Budget 2024. The Indonesian Futures Exchange Supervisory Board (Bappebti) emphasized that the newly established Crude Palm Oil Futures Exchange in Jakarta (ICDX operator), which began trading on Oct 23 with 18 participants, aims to provide a transparent, accountable, and real-time CPO reference price, not to compete with Malaysia's FCPO. The exchange will log local CPO trades in rupiah and may serve as a price reference for taxation. Participation is currently voluntary. The regulatory body is also considering requiring trades to relate only to CPO certified according to Indonesian Sustainable Palm Oil (ISPO) principles in the future, in light of stricter sustainability requirements from the EU and US.
Substitutes & Energy: Malaysian palm oil futures fell, weighed by weakness in rival Dalian vegetable oils and crude oil. Crude oil prices slipped on Monday as diplomatic efforts intensified to contain the Israel-Hamas conflict, making palm oil a less attractive option for biodiesel feedstock. Lacklustre movement in European rapeseed oil markets was also noted. Dalian’s most-active soyoil contract fell 1.13%, while its palm oil contract was down 1.24%. Soyoil prices on the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) rose 0.49%. Malaysia is exploring the use of waste from palm oil processing factories to generate hydrogen gas for renewable energy. US soybeans face increased competition with record global supplies and a strong US dollar.
Market & Technicals: The benchmark palm oil contract for January delivery lost 19 ringgit or 0.5% to 3,752 ringgit ($783.30) a metric ton, opening gap lower following weakness in Chinese vegetable oil futures and a decline in crude oil prices. The contract had risen 0.91% last week, marking its second consecutive weekly gain. The Malaysian ringgit, the contract currency of trade, fell 0.52% against the dollar, hitting its lowest since 1998, which typically makes palm oil more attractive for foreign currency holders.
Forward Views: Hong Leong Investment Bank (HLIB) Research maintained its "neutral" rating on the plantation sector. It lowered its 2023 CPO price assumption by RM150 to RM3,850 per metric tonne (/mt) but raised its 2024 CPO price assumption by RM200 to RM4,000/mt, expecting a recovery from 2024 supported by a favourable palm oil, gas oil (POGO) spread and heightened supply risk from El Nino. HLIB Research's top pick remains IOI Corp Bhd ("buy"; TP: RM4.66).

Date/Timestamp: 2023-10-25
Value: CPO 765.28 USD/tonne; PKO 915.00 USD/tonne
Textual Content:
Supply: Palm oil stockpiles in major producing countries are expected to peak soon, likely by October and November 2023, as the seasonally higher cropping pattern ends. The impact of El Nino on palm production is projected to begin by the end of 1H24 or early 2H24, causing lower rainfall, higher temperatures, and abnormally dry weather in South-East Asia, potentially resulting in lower fresh fruit bunch (FFB) yield through bunch failure, floral abortion, and prolonged male flowering phase. Previous El Nino episodes (2009-2010 and 2015-2016) showed an impact on CPO yield 8-9 months after occurrence. Indonesia, the world's largest producer, averages 7 tonnes of palm oil per hectare a year, compared to the 1.6 tonnes/ha/year yield from relatively wild palm oil trees found in Tanzania. Indonesian investors, through Sampoerna Agro, will help Tanzania boost palm oil output by introducing high-yielding palm tree varieties and agronomic practices, initially focusing on the Kigoma region. Market players anticipate an increase in production and stock levels for October. U.S. farmers had harvested three-quarters of their soybean crop by Sunday, according to USDA data, which was ahead of the five-year average pace, boosting supplies of the oilseed and its products. India reported cumulative normal rainfall of 94.4% of the Long Period Average (LPA) for the entire country, which is 5.6% short of expected normal levels, despite higher-than-average rainfall in September offsetting a deficit in August.
Demand: Malaysian palm oil product exports for Oct 1-20 were estimated to have risen between 7.9% and 9.9% from a month earlier, according to AmSpec Agri Malaysia and Intertek Testing Services. Strong demand for palm oil limited price losses. India’s imports surged to 155 lakh tonnes (lt) during the first 11 months of the oil year (November 2022 to September 2023), driven by a low 5.5% duty on crude palm oil, soyoil, and sunflower oil, and are expected to exceed 165-167 lt for the entire oil year (an increase of 25-27 lt). RBD palmolein imports constitute over 25% of total palm oil imports into India, significantly impacting the domestic refining industry, which is grappling with under-utilised capacity. Tanzania aims for self-sufficiency in cooking oil and for export; currently, 80% of cooking oil consumed in Tanzania is derived from sunflowers.
Policy & Trade: Indonesia is preparing various strategies to deal with the EU Deforestation-free Regulation (EUDR), including revising Presidential Regulation No. 44 of 2022 regarding the Indonesian Sustainable Palm Oil (ISPO) plantation certification system to accommodate broader sustainability provisions. The government is also developing a clearing house for relevant stakeholders and has formed a joint task force with Malaysia and the European Union to address EUDR issues. The first meeting of this task force in August objected to the exclusion of smallholders and sought EU recognition of Indonesia's ISPO sustainability scheme (implemented since 2011). The second meeting is scheduled for December 12. Senior economist Mari Elka Pangestu suggested Indonesia could file a lawsuit against the EU at the World Trade Organization (WTO), viewing EUDR as potential "hidden protectionism," given that the regulation requires products to be deforestation-free after Dec 31, 2020, and necessitates geolocation coordinates. Indonesia, along with 16 other countries (Argentina, Brazil, Bolivia, Colombia, Dominican Republic, Ecuador, Ghana, Guatemala, Honduras, Ivory Coast, Malaysia, Mexico, Nigeria, Paraguay, Peru, and Thailand), sent a joint letter to the EU expressing concerns over EUDR. The Solvent Extractors’ Association of India (SEA) stressed the need for a "bilateral safeguard duty" provision in the revised ASEAN agreement to allow imposition of additional duties when excessive imports harm the domestic industry and to regulate/restrict imports after exporting countries impose export duties, levies, and cess.
Substitutes & Energy: Palm oil futures fell due to weakness in rival Dalian vegetable oils and crude oil prices. Weaker crude prices (both Brent and U.S. West Texas Intermediate futures fell more than 2% on Monday) diminished palm oil’s appeal as a biodiesel feedstock. Dalian's most-active soyoil contract fell 1.9%, while its palm oil contract was down 1.9%. Soyoil prices on the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) fell 1.2%, reaching their lowest price in four months. The palm oil–gas oil (Pogo) spread reversed to negative territory since August 2023, which is expected to support CPO prices by improving blending margins for palm-based biodiesel, thus raising demand prospects.
Market & Technicals: The benchmark palm oil contract for January delivery fell 78 ringgit, or 2.1% to 3,675 ringgit ($769.31) a metric ton. The Malaysian ringgit, palm’s currency of trade, recovered and strengthened 0.3% against the dollar after hitting record lows in the previous session, making palm oil less attractive for foreign currency holders. The CPO price has been trending down recently, bringing the year-to-date average to RM3,866 per tonne, influenced by seasonally higher palm cropping, high vegetable oil stock levels in key consuming countries, and weak demand sentiment for vegetable oils.
Forward Views: Hong Leong Investment Bank (HLIB) Research maintained a "neutral" outlook for the plantation sector. It revised its 2023 CPO price assumption lower by RM150 to RM3,850 per tonne due to recent weak sentiment. HLIB Research raised its 2024 CPO price assumption by RM200 to RM4,000 per tonne, anticipating lower CPO output by the end of 1H24 or early 2H24 to lift CPO price sentiment, supported by a favourable Pogo spread and lagged El Nino impact. IOI Corp Bhd remains its top pick with a target price of RM4.66. The International Palm Oil Congress and Exhibition 2023 (PIPOC 2023), hosted by the Malaysian Palm Oil Board (MPOB) from November 7-9, will discuss the outlook for the oil palm industry, with over 100 speakers and 2,000 participants.

Date/Timestamp: 2023-10-26
Value: CPO 779.32 USD/tonne; PKO 925.00 USD/tonne
Textual Content:
Supply: Palm oil prices fell to a three-month low in September due to seasonally high production in major producing countries in Southeast Asia, according to the FAO. Production estimates by market players suggest a potential 3% to 6% increase for October compared to September, which would lead to already high stocks exceeding 2.313 million metric tonnes. China’s palm oil stocks were around 850,000 metric tonnes as of Oct 20, which is notably high. Sarawak Plantation Bhd secured a RM40 million Islamic facility to partly finance the development and replanting costs of its oil palm plantations in Sarikei, Mukah, Sibu, Niah, and Miri, upgrade the Niah Palm Oil Mill and Mukah Palm Oil Mill, and construct estate buildings and infrastructure. Nigeria, currently the world’s fifth-largest palm oil producer, contributes 1.5% or 1.03 million metric tonnes to the global output (USDA data). Its production reached 1.4 million MT in 2022, a 9% uptick from 1.28 million MT in 2020/21. Edo State, Nigeria, has attracted $531.2 million in investments for greenfield oil palm projects (including ARPN with 12,000ha, Saro Oil Palm with over 10,000ha, and Fayus with 5,000ha), allocated 70,000 hectares of land in four years, and aims for 100,000 hectares for investors and 200,000 hectares for organised plantations by the end of the current administration.
Demand: The Malaysian Palm Oil Council (MPOC) secured RM182 million in estimated potential sales during a visit by African oils and fats companies, conducting 112 meetings with delegations from seven African countries. Buyers sought various palm oil products, highlighting significant opportunities in Sub-Saharan Africa, which accounted for 66% of total oils and fats consumption in 2022 and received 2.3 million tonnes (14.8% of total) of Malaysian palm oil exports in 2022. However, exports of Malaysian palm oil products for Oct 1-25 were estimated to have fallen between 1.1% and 3.1% from a month earlier, according to AmSpec Agri Malaysia and Intertek Testing Services. The outlook for edible oil demand remains challenging due to weak crushing margins and an ample supply of vegetable oil. China's high palm oil stocks (850,000 MT as of Oct 20) suggest it may prioritize existing supplies before further purchases, contributing to bearish sentiment. Despite this, over 50,000 metric tonnes of palm oil were likely sold to India in the past week, with prices ranging from $820 to $847 per metric tonne, indicating demand during the price decline. Nigeria's domestic consumption averages 2.4 million tons per year, with a demand of 2.7 million metric tonnes yearly, leading to an import shortfall. Nigeria imported N299.6 billion worth of palm oil from 2017 to 2022. Imports from Malaysia surged 353% in Jan-April 2023, reaching 92,961 MT from 20,513 MT in the corresponding period of 2022.
Policy & Trade: The Indonesian government is preparing strategies to deal with the EU Deforestation-free Regulation (EUDR), including revising Presidential Regulation No. 44 of 2022 on the Indonesian Sustainable Palm Oil (ISPO) certification system to expand its sustainability provisions. A clearing house is being developed for stakeholders, and a joint task force with Malaysia and the EU, whose first meeting in August objected to smallholder exclusion and sought EU recognition of the ISPO scheme, is scheduled for a second meeting on December 12. Cargill is set to become one of the first large-scale US suppliers to exclusively offer palm oil certified by the Roundtable for Sustainable Palm Oil (RSPO) from October, ceasing conventional palm oil offerings in its US portfolio. By January 2024, all customers from Cargill’s US refineries will receive RSPO-certified palm oil. Palm oil is among the top five agricultural products imported into Nigeria, despite being on a forex exclusion list since June 2015 by the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN). The Edo State Oil Palm Programme Bill has passed its second reading, aiming to provide a legal framework for the industry and regulate production activities. Governor Obaseki is committed to RSPO principles, partnered with Pro-Forest to audit forest assets, and is establishing a technical committee and forestry commission.
Substitutes & Energy: There has been a slight decline in oilseeds prices, alongside a larger drop for soy oil, as harvests pressure the market in the face of slow demand. Chicago soybean spot futures registered a net decline of 1% over the month. US export demand for soybeans was soft, partly linked to competition from Brazilian suppliers. Gulf export quotations for soy retreated by 2% to $512 fob, while Brazilian old crop supplies were offered at an atypical discount, with export quotations (Paranagua) declining by 4% to $491 fob. Argentina Up River values held steady at $521 fob. ICE canola futures in Canada retreated by 3% month-on-month. Palm oil prices fell to a three-month low, and sunflowerseed oil is currently trading at an unusual discount. The FAO’s Food Price Index reported that the world price of vegetable oil was down by an average 3.9% in September (second consecutive fall), driven by lower prices across palm, sunflower, soy, and rapeseed oils. International sunflower oil quotations declined markedly due to harvest pressure in the Black Sea region and robust farmer selling. Rapeseed oil prices declined on abundant global export supplies, while world soy oil prices followed suit despite prospects of firm demand from the biodiesel sector. Oil benchmark Brent held above $88, but benchmark prices fell in each of the previous three sessions.
Market & Technicals: The benchmark palm oil contract for January delivery rose 15 ringgit, or 0.4%, to 3,682 ringgit ($770.78) per metric ton at closing. A strengthening Malaysian ringgit (0.1% against the dollar) capped gains. US dollar firmness has been a consistent feature affecting soy markets.
Forward Views: Mintec anticipates continued stability in production trends for the remainder of 2023 and expects stocks to remain at current high levels, which would continue to suppress palm oil prices unless a significant buying surge occurs. The Edo Palm Oil programme aims to eliminate palm oil imports in Nigeria within the next five years and potentially make Nigeria a world leader in palm oil production in less than 10 years with special grants.

- The Malaysian ringgit strengthened 1.97% against the dollar, making the commodity more expensive for buyers holding foreign currencies.

Date/Timestamp: 2023-11-08
Value: CPO 793.79 USD/tonne; PKO 930.00 USD/tonne
Textual Content:
Supply
- Malaysian palm oil futures closed lower for the third consecutive session, partly due to prospects of higher supplies. Anilkumar Bagani, commodity research head at Sunvin Group, stated that growth in palm oil production is "much higher than the market estimate of a 2-3% increase."
- End stocks in Malaysia were nearly 10% higher at the end of October compared to September, as production surpassed exports and consumption (Anilkumar Bagani). Malaysia’s palm oil stocks at the end of October were at their highest since May 2019 (Reuters survey).
- Global palm oil output is likely to drop next year due to El Niño, with Indonesia's output seen dropping at least 1 million metric tons next year, while Malaysia's output is seen unchanged (Dorab Mistry).
- Malaysia, a major palm oil producer, generates millions of tonnes of Palm Oil Mill Effluent (POME) annually, which is being converted into biogas through anaerobic digestion. The organic content within POME is also transformed into a nutrient-rich fertilizer.
- The MPOB International Palm Oil Congress and Exhibition (PIPOC 2023) is ongoing from November 7-9, 2023.
Demand
- Malaysia aims to increase its export value of palm oil to China above RM14 billion this year (Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof). In 2022, China was Malaysia's second-largest palm oil export market, importing 3.14 million tonnes worth RM14.86 billion, accounting for 11.2% of the country's total palm oil exports.
- CPO demand is expected to increase slightly ahead of upcoming festive seasons, including Deepavali in India, and Chinese New Year, Ramadhan, and Hari Raya Aidilfitri for China and Muslim countries (MPOB Director-General Datuk Ahmad Parveez Ghulam Kadir).
- Global consumption of oils and fats is on a steady rise, with palm oil poised to play a pivotal role in ensuring worldwide food security (Malaysian Palm Oil Council director Faisal Iqbal). Malaysia contributes approximately 23.3% to global palm oil production and holds a significant 31.1% share in global palm oil exports. Markets in ASEAN, the Middle East, and African regions show consistent growth and are markets of interest for Malaysian suppliers.
Policy & Trade
- 15 Malaysian palm oil associations reiterated their call for a review of the windfall profit levy (WPL) on oil palm planters.
- The National Energy Transition Roadmap (NETR) has identified bioenergy, derived from palm waste, as a catalyst for energy transition. The energy generated from POME can earn Renewable Energy Certificates (RECs), creating a fresh revenue stream for palm oil producers.
- Malaysia's Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry announced that the maximum retail prices of bottled pure palm cooking oil for the period of November 8 to December 7 will remain unchanged: 1kg bottle at RM6.90, 2kg at RM13.30, 3kg at RM19.60, and 5kg at RM30.90. This decision aims to ease the cost of living and prevent unreasonable price increases.
- Julau MP Larry Sng suggested focusing international lobbying efforts in Europe and the US to counter anti-palm oil campaigns, as these regions influence global laws. He stated that the RM15 million allocated in the 2024 budget for lobbying is inadequate, as lobbying for palm oil in England, Europe, and the US costs a total of RM15.5 million a year.
- Malaysia and Indonesia have teamed up to protect palm oil products threatened by the European Union's Deforestation Regulation (EUDR), which will ban imports from land deforested after December 31, 2020, starting January next year. The EU is the third-largest market for both countries.
- The government has rescheduled the transition period of the Malaysian Sustainable Palm Oil (MSPO) 2015 (MSPO 1.0) standards to the revised MSPO 2022 (MSPO 2.0) from August 2023 to December 2024, providing companies and smallholders a 17-month period to upgrade their practices to the eight-part MSPO 2.0 standards.
- The Council of Palm Oil Producing Countries (CPOPC) conducted a working visit to Italy, the Netherlands, and Belgium for engagements on the EUDR. CPOPC proposed an inception phase for a smooth transition and consultative engagement during the drafting of implementing acts to ensure pragmatic guidelines. They also called for clear methodology and transparent data for benchmarking.
Substitutes & Energy
- Dalian's most-active soyoil contract fell 0.3%, while its palm oil contract was up 0.03%. Soyoil prices on the Chicago Board of Trade fell 1.1%.
- China imported 5.16 million metric tons of soybeans in October, a 25% surge from a year earlier but lower than analysts’ expectations. Refinitiv Commodities Research expects delayed October cargoes to arrive in November, lifting November imports to 12 million metric tons.
- A rapidly progressing U.S. soybean harvest, 91% done (behind the 92% average estimate but ahead of the five-year average of 86%), weighed on prices.
Market & Technicals
- The benchmark palm oil contract for January delivery on the Bursa Malaysia Derivatives Exchange fell 35 ringgit (0.9%) to 3,719 ringgit ($796.70) a metric ton at closing, marking a third consecutive session of decline.
- The Malaysian ringgit weakened 0.8% against the dollar, which limited losses by making palm oil more attractive for foreign currency holders.
Forward Views
- MPOB Director-General Datuk Ahmad Parveez Ghulam Kadir expects CPO to hover around RM4,000 per tonne this year, with little change to Malaysia’s production compared to 2022. He hopes production will exceed 2022's 18.5 million tonnes. He noted El Niño effects are expected in the next six months.

Date/Timestamp: 2023-11-09
Value: CPO 786.93 USD/tonne; PKO 910.00 USD/tonne
Textual Content:
Supply
- Smallholders account for 28% of Malaysia's total area for palm oil production.
- Almost 100% of palm oil estates and mills operating in Malaysia have obtained the Malaysian Sustainable Palm Oil (MSPO) certification (Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim).
- Malaysia, the world's second-largest palm oil producer, accounted for 31% of the 87.39 million tonnes of palm oil produced globally in 2022, from only about 5.67 million hectares of planted area (less than 2% of the total 312 million hectares for oilseed crops production globally). Palm oil is the most productive vegetable oil, yielding at least four to five times more oil per hectare than other vegetable oils.
- MPOB research in breeding and biotechnology, including clonal palm series and genome programs, has enhanced yields and reduced contamination risks. Mechanisation has improved plantation management efficiency.
- There are 660,000 hectares (roughly 11.6% of the total oil palm planted area) with trees aged 25 years or older, necessitating immediate replanting. If the current replanting rate, which is less than 2% of the total planted area per year, continues, the aged palm area will expand to 770,000ha by 2027 (Malaysian Palm Oil Association, MPOA, data).
Demand
- Malaysian palm oil futures rose due to robust soybean imports to China and indications of strong demand.
- China imported 5.16 million metric tons of soybeans in October, a 25% surge from a year earlier (though lower than analysts' expectations). China also booked its largest single-day U.S. soybean purchases in three months.
- Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof aims to strengthen trade in palm oil during his official visit to China, starting this Sunday, expecting to further increase palm oil exports. China was Malaysia’s second-largest palm oil export market in 2022, accounting for 11.2% of total Malaysian palm oil exports, with a total export value of palm oil and palm-based products to China rising 12.9% to RM14.86 billion in 2022 from RM13.16 billion in 2021.
Policy & Trade
- Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim launched the Sawit Intelligent Management System (SIMS), developed by MPOB, designed to facilitate transactional data management along the palm oil supply chain, enhancing industry efficiency and cost savings.
- PM Anwar stated that the allocation of incentives for oil palm replanting programs (RM100 million in Budget 2024) may be increased if companies can prove they will work with smallholders. This incentive is for 7,000 independent oil palm smallholders to increase productivity by replanting old trees with new breeds.
- PM Anwar urged the European Union (EU) for a fair and balanced implementation of the EU Deforestation-free Regulation (EUDR). He emphasized Malaysia's proactive and responsible steps to safeguard palm oil production and expected EU appreciation and recognition for efforts by Malaysia and Indonesia. Thailand's Prime Minister Srettha Thavisin has also assured cooperation with Malaysia and Indonesia in presenting their case to the EU.
- The EUDR will affect Malaysian agricultural commodity products, primarily palm oil, timber, cocoa, and rubber exports, starting January next year. Malaysia and Indonesia have established an ad hoc joint task force with the EU to address apprehensions about the EUDR's impact on producers, especially smallholders.
- Malaysia's mandatory MSPO certification scheme, introduced in 2015, was revised to MSPO 2022, focusing on transparency, safety, employment conditions, environment, biodiversity, and ecosystem protection.
- Malaysia has been committed to sustainable energy since the 1980s, pioneering palm-based biodiesel technology. The government established the Mechanisation and Automation Research Consortium of Oil Palm in 2021 with MPOB to address labor shortages and promotes tax incentives for automation.
- MSPO certification has gained global recognition, being adopted for the Tokyo 2020 Olympics and Paralympic Games Sustainable Sourcing Code, accepted by Japan's Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry for renewable energy, and promoted by Panpan Foods at the 2022 Beijing Winter Olympics.
- The oil palm sector contributed RM137.89 billion in export earnings for palm oil and palm-based products in 2022, up from RM108.52 billion in 2021.
- Deputy PM Fadillah Yusof's visit to China also aims to strengthen bilateral relations, coinciding with the 50th anniversary of Malaysia-China diplomatic relations next year.
Substitutes & Energy
- Soyoil prices on the Chicago Board of Trade rose 0.4%. Dalian's most-active soyoil contract was up 0.15%, while its palm oil contract was up 0.1%.
- Oil prices stuttered after sliding to their lowest in over three months in the previous session, weighed down by concerns over waning demand. Weaker crude oil prices make palm oil a less attractive option for biodiesel feedstock.
Market & Technicals
- The benchmark palm oil contract FCPOc3 for January delivery on the Bursa Malaysia Derivatives Exchange rose 46 ringgit (1.2%) to 3,766 ringgit ($807.12) a metric ton at the midday break.
- The Malaysian ringgit last traded flat against the dollar.
Forward Views
- Global production of palm oil is expected to reach 81.44 million tonnes in 2023, increasing by almost 3%.

Date/Timestamp: 2023-11-10
Value: CPO 791.27 USD/tonne; PKO 940.00 USD/tonne
Textual Content:
Supply
- El Niño remains a key wild card for CPO prices in 2024, with its impact on palm oil yield expected to be delayed by 10-12 months, with the first signs likely to occur during the second half of 2024 (Ivy Ng, CIMB Investment Bank). Factors such as ageing estates, lower fertiliser input in 2022, and ongoing climate change could exacerbate El Niño's impact.
- Production is expected to be flat or decline in 2024 in Malaysia and Indonesia, depending on rainfall during the current El Niño (Julian McGill, Glenauk Economics).
- Thomas Mielke of Oil World expects Indonesian palm oil output to stagnate in 2024, and Malaysian production to be near 18.4 million tonnes.
- Ivy Ng expects Malaysia to contribute 18.2 million tonnes to global supply, with Indonesia leading with 48 million tonnes. Lower yields from aging palm oil estates, El Niño impact, reduced fertiliser input in prior years, and lower productivity from new workers will affect palm oil supply in 2024 (Ivy Ng).
- India's IVPA President Sudhakar Desai forecasts Malaysia's palm oil production to increase to 18.85 million tonnes for the oil year 2023-24 (November to October), an increase of 240,000 tonnes from 18.61 million tonnes the previous year. Indonesia’s production is expected to remain steady at 49.26 million tonnes.
- Malaysia is expected to see a stock build-up of approximately 2.7 million tonnes, but the market is anticipated to transition to tighter end stocks by April-May 2024 (Sudhakar Desai).
- Ukraine's sunflower seed production is expected to perform better in 2023/2024, potentially surpassing pre-war export levels due to increased crushing activities despite the cancellation of the Black Sea Grain Initiative. However, Ukrainian crushers are holding back seeds due to low prices and margins.
Demand
- Indian vegetable oil imports are forecast to be around 16.20 million tonnes for the oil year 2023-24 (November to October), with palm oil imports expected to reach 9 million tonnes and soft oils around 7.12 million tonnes (Sudhakar Desai, IVPA). Indian imports hit a record 16.9 million tonnes during the oil year 2022-23 due to attractive low prices, which stimulated stock build-up and consumption rebound. Total Indian consumption could reach 25.20 million tonnes with a normal growth of approximately 2.8% in 2023-24.
- Meal demand is not growing sufficiently quickly to absorb additional output, particularly once Argentina's crush recovers (Julian McGill).
- Big increases in palm oil exports in recent months resulted in large stocks in India and other importing countries, now leading to temporarily reduced palm oil imports in October-December 2023 (Thomas Mielke).
- Global edible oil stock usage is expected to decline from 14.4% to 13.8% in 2024 (Ivy Ng).
- The full implementation of Indonesia's B35 mandate is expected to increase biodiesel demand, potentially adding at least 1 million tonnes of additional usage in 2024 (Ivy Ng).
- Palm oil has faced strong competition from other edible oils, particularly sunflower oil, which saw increased flow from the Black Sea into countries like India and the Middle East, exerting pressure on CPO prices (Dr Sathia Varqa, Palm Oil Analytics).
- Ongoing high production in Malaysia and high stocks in China and India are considered bearish on CPO prices in the short term (Dr Sathia Varqa).
Policy & Trade
- Indonesia has adopted the B35 biodiesel mandate.
- The Marine Police Force (MPF) foiled an attempt to smuggle out 4,216kg of cooking oil, estimated to be worth RM10,540, via the waters off Semporna. The subsidised cooking oil is believed to have been intended for a neighboring country, with investigations referred to the Semporna Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry (KPDN) under the Control of Supply Act 1961.
- Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim urged the European Union (EU) to recognize and appreciate the efforts of palm oil producing countries in meeting the EU Deforestation-free Regulation (EUDR).
Substitutes & Energy
- Robust crude oil prices, driven by geopolitical risks, are expected to support biodiesel demand (Ivy Ng).
- Sunflower oil prices declined sharply due to high sunflower seed stock in Russia and the assumption of trade from Ukrainian ports. However, sunflower oil prices cannot continue to fall indefinitely as it would halt crushing activities.
- Global edible oil supply growth is lower (Thomas Mielke).
- Increases in soybean crush are expected to lead to higher oil prices in 2024 (Julian McGill).
Market & Technicals
- For the first 10 months of 2023, the average CPO prices saw a year-on-year (y-o-y) drop of 23% to RM3,835 per tonne compared with RM5,352 per tonne in the same period a year ago. For the third quarter of 2023, CPO price declined by 4.6% y-o-y and 1% quarter-on-quarter to RM3,811 per tonne (Ivy Ng).
- CPO prices are averaging at about RM3,875 for 2023, hovering between RM3,800 and RM3,900 per tonne towards the end of the year (Ivy Ng).
- Palm oil was not the cheapest oil for some parts of the year and was trading at a premium to rapeseed oil in certain months (Dr Sathia Varqa).
- Prices are down by 25% to 30% on a year-to-date basis (Dr Sathia Varqa).
- The Bursa Malaysia Derivatives (BMD) is expected to fluctuate within the range of Malaysian ringgit 3,600-3,900 for the next three months (Sudhakar Desai).
Forward Views
- Palm oil industry experts remain optimistic for a recovery in crude palm oil (CPO) prices, which are expected to surpass the RM4,000 per tonne mark in 2024.
- Julian McGill, managing director of Glenauk Economics, expects CPO prices to climb to RM4,000 per tonne by the first quarter of 2024.
- Thomas Mielke, executive director of Oil World, expects palm oil prices, currently close to their lows, to rise by US$100-US$150 within the next four to six months in 2024 and 2025 due to insufficient supplies and lower growth in other edible oils. He also noted that price volatility has increased and is expected to remain high.
- Ivy Ng (CIMB Investment Bank) expects global edible oil stock and usage to decline in 2024, projecting CPO prices to move up from RM3,870 to RM4,100 per tonne for 2024. She anticipates the current El Niño news to have a more pronounced impact on CPO prices in the second half of 2024, once current high stocks are reduced and Indonesia's B35 implementation has gained traction.
- Dr Sathia Varqa (Palm Oil Analytics) expects CPO prices to average at about RM3,800 per tonne this year, lower than last year's historic highs. He projects prices to build on the recovery into the first quarter of 2024, trading to a high of RM4,000 to RM4,200 per tonne. He identifies supply risk from weather, sunflower oil pricing, and ongoing geopolitical tension as the three main swing factors in CPO pricing for November-December 2023 and 2024.
- Sudhakar Desai (IVPA) hinted at the possibility of prices rising to Malaysian ringgit 4,200 by March due to the tightening stock situation, particularly in Malaysia.

Date/Timestamp: 2023-11-14
Value: CPO 810.17 USD/tonne; PKO 970.00 USD/tonne
Textual Content:
Supply:
*   Malaysia's palm oil stocks at the end of October rose 5.84% from the previous month to 2.45 million metric tons, according to the Malaysian Palm Oil Board (MPOB). This figure was below a Reuters survey forecast of 2.56 million tons (10.82% growth).
*   Crude palm oil production in Malaysia gained 5.89% month-on-month to 1.94 million tonnes in October (MPOB), which was above a Reuters survey forecast of 1.88 million tons.
*   Higher edible oil imports lifted vegetable oil stocks in India to 3.3 million tons on November 1, up from 2.46 million tons a year ago, as reported by the Solvent Extractors' Association of India (SEA).
Demand:
*   Malaysian palm oil exports increased to 1.47 million tonnes in October (MPOB), which was above a Reuters survey forecast of 1.29 million tons.
*   India's palm oil imports in the 2022/23 marketing year (ended Oct 31) surged 24% to a record 9.79 million metric tons, and sunflower oil imports rose 54% to a record 3 million tons (SEA). This surge was driven by a rebound in consumption and steep discounts compared to rival soyoil.
*   Total edible oil imports in India for 2022/23 surged to a record 16.47 million tons, up 17.4% year-on-year. Higher Indian purchases could help lower palm oil stocks in Indonesia and Malaysia.
*   India's palm oil imports in October fell 15% from the previous month to 708,706 tons, the lowest in 4 months (SEA). Indian refiners had bought aggressively during November-January and July-September but slashed imports in October due to higher stocks, according to Rajesh Patel of GGN Research.
*   Malaysia, via the MPOB, will continue research and development to increase palm oil-based value-added products for Chinese companies to export to Muslim regions in China, with several products already commercialized. Chinese companies are replacing other raw materials with palm oil to cater to the global Islamic market.
*   Interband Group of Companies senior palm oil trader Jim Teh reckons buyers, especially from India, had already secured their stocks early before the long holiday break.
Policy & Trade:
*   Malaysia's Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof is on an official visit to China (Nov 12-19) to strengthen cooperation in R&D and promote the Malaysian Sustainable Palm Oil (MSPO) certification scheme. MPOB plans to meet China’s agriculture minister to seek recognition of MSPO for Chinese products.
*   The Indian government's move to cut the import tax on edible oils to 5.5% encouraged overseas buying. The tax was not raised after global prices fell, making edible oil cheaper and boosting consumption.
*   Indonesian Ambassador to Malaysia Datuk Hermono noted strengthening bilateral economic ties, with bilateral trade value between Indonesia and Malaysia in 2022 at US$28.5 billion. However, he anticipates a 20-30% reduction to an estimated US$22 billion by year-end 2023 (US$17.5 billion as of Sept 2023) due to a noticeable drop in commodity prices, particularly coal and crude palm oil.
*   Indonesia's upcoming elections in February 2024 have led to a "wait-and-see" approach from foreign investors regarding future investments.
Substitutes & Energy:
*   India's soyoil imports in 2022/23 fell 12% to 3.68 million tons as it traded at a premium over palm oil and sunflower oil for most months. Soyoil imports in October slumped 62% from September to 135,325 tons (lowest in 34 months), and sunflower oil dropped 49% to 153,780 tons (lowest in 7 months).
*   Weakness in the crude oil market dampened the local palm oil market for the week ended November 10.
*   Indonesia's largest export to Malaysia, coal, has seen a noticeable drop in price.
Market & Technicals:
*   The CPO futures contract on Bursa Malaysia Derivatives was expected to see profit-taking this week, with prices seen moving between RM3,400 and RM3,650 per tonne. Speculators were also expected to take a break during the festive season, leading to a quieter market.
*   The market was closed for Deepavali on November 13, with operations resuming on November 14.
*   For the week just ended (Nov 10), the local market traded mostly lower, dampened by low buying interest and weak market sentiment due to concerns over rising production and weakness in crude oil.
*   On a weekly basis (for the week ended Nov 10), the November 2023 contract added RM41 to RM3,673 per tonne; December 2023 gained RM20 to RM3,737; January 2024 rose RM34 to RM3,802; February 2024 bagged RM40 to RM3,839; March 2024 went up RM50 to RM3,855; and April 2024 gained RM56 to RM3,852.
*   Total weekly volume improved to 248,880 lots from 163,201 lots in the preceding week, while open interest was slightly higher at 215,538 contracts from 215,228 contracts previously.
*   The physical CPO price for November South gained RM21 to RM3,700 per tonne from RM3,679 in the previous week.
*   The export value of palm-based products from Malaysia to China in 2022 totaled RM16.41 billion, while the export value of Malaysian palm oil to China in the same year was RM8.44 billion.
*   MPOB's Palm Oil Research and Technical Service Institute (Portsim) has received accreditation from the China National Accreditation Services (CNAS) and the China Inspection Body and Laboratory Mandatory Approval (CMA).
Forward Views:
*   Interband Group's Jim Teh expects CPO futures to see profit-taking this week, with prices between RM3,400 and RM3,650 per tonne.
*   Portsim foresees the vegan market, particularly for new products like vegan meat, growing in China and Europe.
*   Portsim is researching health products based on the versatile crop tocotrienol.

Date/Timestamp: 2023-11-15
Value: CPO 837.09 USD/tonne; PKO 990.00 USD/tonne
Textual Content:
Supply:
*   Malaysia's palm oil stocks at the end of October were 2.45 million tonnes, the highest in four years, having climbed for the sixth straight month (MPOB, HLIB Research, RHB Research).
*   Production figures for October were 1.94 million metric tonnes, increasing 5.9% month-on-month, with Peninsular Malaysia and East Malaysia contributions rising 6.3% and 5.4% respectively (HLIB Research). Year-to-date production increased marginally to 15.2 million metric tonnes as fresh fruit bunch (FFB) yield continued to trend up since July.
*   Hong Leong Investment Bank (HLIB Research) believes palm oil stockpiles peaked in October and began trending down from November, as production should have peaked last month.
*   However, Maybank Investment Bank (Maybank IB) Research gathers that production will likely stay robust in November, suggesting the monthly local stockpile may not peak for 2023. RHB Research also expects Malaysian palm oil production to taper off in the coming months.
*   Rain deficits in Indonesia's key palm oil producing areas may cause delays in the 2024 fresh fruit bunch harvest (Kenanga Research). Indonesia's weather bureau reported rainfall in parts of Sumatra and Kalimantan declining since July, potentially delaying crop ripening, and Indonesian production peak may be delayed to 2024; production declined 11.5% month-on-month in August (RHB Research).
*   The ongoing El Niño in 2023 is considered mild thus far, with a minor impact on 2024's overall CPO output (Maybank IB Research). The US National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration stated El Niño conditions plateaued in mid-October at a moderate level, while the Australian Bureau of Meteorology indicates a 60% probability of a strong El Niño with a median Nino 3.4 Index forecast at 1.9 (RHB Research).
*   Planters' margins are expected to improve due to lower costs, with average fertiliser prices having fallen by 30% year-on-year (Kenanga Research).
Demand:
*   Malaysia's Deputy Prime Minister Fadillah Yusof expressed confidence that Malaysia’s exports of palm oil and related products to China will increase further this year, driven by growing demand from China’s oleochemical and animal feed sectors. Last year, exports to China reached US$3.72 billion or RM14.86 billion, representing 11.4% of Malaysia's total worldwide palm derivatives exports (RM130.25 billion).
*   HLIB Research expects exports to be subdued in the near term as the winter season approaches, which typically weakens demand for palm oil, also citing relatively high stockpiles in key importing countries and the absence of major festive seasons.
*   Malaysia's exports in October increased for the first time since July by 21% to 1.47 million metric tonnes, attributed to restocking activities from China.
*   Kenanga Research anticipates edible oil demand for 2023 to revert to its usual 3-4% year-on-year trend line growth, likely persisting into 2024 due to robust demand for food and biodiesel.
*   Analysts cited a lack of notable demand catalysts for the plantation sector. RHB Research expects weakening demand in the export market given high stock levels.
Policy & Trade:
*   Indonesia's leading presidential candidate, Prabowo Subianto, stated that Indonesia doesn't "really need Europe anymore," criticizing the EU's ban on some Indonesian imports (soy, palm oil, coffee, cocoa, timber, rubber, beef from Dec 2024) unless deforestation-free proof is provided. He suggested Indonesia should align more closely with Asian nations like Japan, South Korea, China, and India. These comments precede the next round of EU-Indonesia free trade agreement talks in December.
*   Malaysia's Deputy Prime Minister Fadillah Yusof continued his official visit to China (Nov 12-19) to strengthen cooperation in R&D and capacity building, and promote MSPO certification, including initiatives for new palm-based products (nutraceutical, pharmaceutical, red palm oil).
Substitutes & Energy:
*   Crude oil prices have fallen 16% in the last four weeks (RHB Research), causing the palm oil-gas oil (POGO) spread to turn negative, thereby reducing chances of discretionary biodiesel demand (2.5-3.0 million tonnes) returning to the market.
*   HLIB Research noted narrower palm oil and gas oil spreads, and CPO discounts to soybeans, as factors curbing near-term demand.
*   UOB KayHian noted constrained supply of alternative vegetable oils.
Market & Technicals:
*   A weak Malaysian ringgit has been a key price supporting factor for CPO futures on Bursa Malaysia Derivatives over the past six months, and Maybank IB Research expects this to persist into 2024, although it could add to cost pressures for local planters.
Forward Views:
*   Analysts are mostly "neutral" on the plantation sector, citing high October palm oil stockpile and lack of demand catalysts.
*   CPO prices are pegged at RM3,800 to RM3,900 per tonne for 2023, with optimism for prices to climb above RM4,000 per tonne by Q1 2024 on a better export outlook.
*   UOB KayHian expects CPO prices to trade between 3,800 ringgit (805 U.S. dollars) to 4,200 ringgit (890 U.S. dollars) per ton from December 2023 to Q1 2024, influenced by the intensifying El Niño and constrained supply of alternative vegetable oils. They maintained CPO price assumptions at 4,000 ringgit per ton for 2023 and 4,200 ringgit per ton for 2024.
*   Maybank IB Research raised its 2023 and 2024 CPO average selling price (ASP) forecasts by 100 ringgit and 200 ringgit to 3,800 ringgit and 3,700 ringgit per tonne, respectively. This revision reflects the anticipated impact on 2024 CPO output due to the ongoing mild El Niño episode and expected weak ringgit.
*   MIDF Research forecasts that average local CPO delivery prices will close 1.7% month-on-month higher to 3,702 ringgit per ton in November, anticipating normal production in Q1 2023 but a gradual decline in drier months in Q2 2024. Hence, CPO prices are expected to hinge on the high side in H1 2024.
*   RHB Research maintained its "neutral" rating on the sector with a tactically positive trading strategy, keeping 3,900 ringgit per tonne CPO price assumptions for 2023 and 2024. They continue to prefer Malaysian planters over regional players.
*   Kenanga Research likes Kuala Lumpur Kepong Bhd (target price RM24.50) and PPB Group Bhd (target price RM19.30). RHB Research's top local-planter picks include IOI Corp Bhd, Sarawak Oil Palms Bhd and Ta Ann Holdings Bhd, while regional picks include Golden Agri-Resources Ltd and Perusahaan Perkebunan London Sumatra Indonesia Tbk PT.
*   RHB Research expects El Niño to impact productivity more significantly from late Q2 2024, thereby pushing estimated crude palm oil prices higher in the second half of 2024.

Date/Timestamp: 2023-11-16
Value: CPO 840.46 USD/tonne; PKO 990.00 USD/tonne
Textual Content:
Supply:
*   Biomicrogels Group (BMG) introduced two new products, Biomicrogel BMG-C4 and BMG-SPO, for palm oil factories in Malaysia. These products aim to optimize existing oil extraction processes, significantly increasing productivity, reducing losses, and minimizing water consumption. BMG estimates mills can add over US$500,000 annually to operating profit using these products. The products are biodegradable.
*   Malaysia's palm oil stockpiles were at a four-year high at the end of October despite more-than-expected exports.
Demand:
*   Malaysia's Deputy Prime Minister Fadillah Yusof expressed confidence that Malaysia’s exports of palm oil and related products to China will increase further this year, particularly from China’s rapidly growing oleochemical and animal feed sectors. Malaysia shipped US$3.72 billion (RM14.86 billion) worth of the commodity and related products to China last year, accounting for 11% of its total worldwide exports of palm derivatives. China has been Malaysia’s largest trading partner for 14 years.
*   India's imports of palm oil and sunflower oil in 2022/23 surged 24% and 54%, respectively, to record highs.
Policy & Trade:
*   Malaysia's Deputy Prime Minister Fadillah Yusof (also Plantation and Commodities Minister) stated that the Malaysian Sustainable Palm Oil (MSPO) certification is gaining global recognition and is perceived to be on par with the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil (RSPO), with India having recognized it. He expressed hope for further global recognition.

In 2022, Sabah's palm oil production was 4.29 million tonnes, contributing 5.76% of global palm oil production. 26% of Sabah’s 1.51 million hectares of oil palm planted areas are RSPO certified. Smallholders contribute significantly to oil palm areas in Indonesia and Malaysia, accounting for around 40%, yet only about 170,000 out of over seven million global small-scale growers are RSPO-certified. Deforestation rates have reportedly fallen in Malaysia and Indonesia in recent years. The RSPO aims to reduce emissions and tackle climate change, emphasizing improved soil carbon and cut methane releases from palm oil mills. India's National Mission on Edible Oils-Oil Palm (NMEO-OP) aims to increase the area under oil palm cultivation aggressively from the current 3.70 lakh hectares towards a potential area of 28 lakh hectares.
- Demand: Malaysia exported approximately 25 million tonnes of palm oil and palm-based products in 2022. India's palm oil imports in November jumped 22.8% from the previous month to 869,491 metric tons, reaching a three-month high, driven by refiners preferring palm oil over rival soyoil and sunflower oil due to steep discounts. Domestic stocks of vegetable oil in India fell to 2.96 million tons by December 1, from 3.14 million tons a month earlier. India imports around nine million tonnes of palm oil annually, valued at approximately Rs 40,000 crore, which constitutes about 56% of its total edible oil imports.
- Policy & Trade: Malaysia introduced the Malaysian Sustainable Palm Oil (MSPO) certification scheme in 2015, making it mandatory from January 1, 2020. Malaysian palm oil biofuel exporters also meet German ISCC standards. Sabah has achieved Step 1 of the RSPO's jurisdictional approach to certified sustainable palm oil, with a government goal of 100% RSPO certified palm oil by 2025. The RSPO completed a five-year review of standards, with changes expected by mid-2024, and no-deforestation rules will not be watered down. The European Union and the United States are increasingly turning to regulation instead of relying on voluntary standards like RSPO. Thailand's Energy Policy Committee decided on December 13 to simplify diesel oil offerings from May 1, 2024, to only B7 (6.6-7% biodiesel) and B20 (19-20% biodiesel), terminating B10 sales. India's Narendra Modi government launched the National Mission on Edible Oils-Oil Palm (NMEO-OP) in August 2021, allocating Rs 11,040 crore to encourage domestic oilseeds production, including substantially increased subsidies and the first-time introduction of a viability price for fresh fruit bunches.
- Substitutes & Energy: Indian refiners opted for palm oil over soyoil and sunflower oil due to steep discounts. In November, soyoil imports increased 10.8% to 149,894 tons, while sunflower oil imports fell 16.3% to a 17-month low of 128,707 tons.
- Forward Views: The Malaysian Palm Oil Council (MPOC) indicates Malaysia's oil palm industry aligns with the 12th Malaysia Plan (12MP) for carbon neutrality by as early as 2050. RSPO adviser M.R. Chandran stated that reducing emissions and tackling climate change will be crucial in the coming decades. A Mumbai-based trader expects India's palm oil imports to decrease in December due to reduced discounts compared to soyoil and the tendency for tropical oil to solidify in winter. A New-Delhi-based dealer anticipates soyoil imports will rise in December due to increased competitiveness after recent price drops. Thailand's Department of Energy Business expects daily consumption of biodiesel and palm oil to increase to 4.66 million litres and 3.88 million kg, respectively, next year. India's NMEO-OP targets an increase in oil palm area to 10 lakh hectares by 2025-26 (an additional 6.50 lakh ha from 2019-20's 3.5 lakh ha), with 3.28 lakh ha in the North-Eastern states, aiming for 66 lakh tonnes of fresh fruit bunches (FFBs) and 11.20 lakh tonnes of crude palm oil production by 2025-26 (from 0.27 lakh tonnes in 2019-20).

Plantation and Commodities Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani stated the ministry is considering incorporating palm oil harvesting into Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) programmes to address labour shortages in the sector, suggesting a salary range of RM3,000 to RM4,000 plus commission-based incentives for local harvesters. The government has proposed expanding the scope of automation tax incentives to include the plantation sector to reduce labour dependence through mechanisation and automation. The Council of Palm Oil Producing Countries (CPOPC) plans to collaborate with other vegetable oil producers to address sustainability issues via a "triple-track approach," aiming to enhance global perception of palm oil's sustainability and its role in assisting developing countries to achieve the United Nations (UN) Sustainable Development Goals. This includes organizing the 2024 Sustainable Vegetable Oils Conference (SVOC), utilizing CPOPC's observer status in the Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC) for participation in UN activities (Partnership Forum, High-level Political Forum on Sustainable Development, UN ESCAP Asia-Pacific Forum, UNFCCC COP 29, and a joint event with FAO), and plans to expand memberships by conducting visits to Thailand, Africa, and Latin America, along with joint missions to China and South Asia countries. Indonesia's state-owned palm oil planter, PalmCo, plans to invest in a biodiesel plant. Deputy Minister of Plantation and Commodities Datuk Chan Foong Hin hopes for full MSPO certification status in Sabah to ensure the reputation of Malaysian palm oil products.

Substitutes & Energy: Oil World projects global oils and fats consumption to rise, driven by increased biodiesel mandate requirements in the US, Indonesia, and Brazil. Soybean production is expected to remain tight at least until April 2024.

MPOC forecasts a deficit of 0.24 million tonnes in Indonesia's palm oil supply as domestic consumption for biodiesel and food is expected to increase by 0.64 million tonnes with no expected growth in production; this deficit could further expand if exports exceed forecasted levels. MPOC projects Malaysian palm oil production in 2024 to see a growth of 1%, reaching 18.75 million tonnes, expecting the Q4 2023 production trend to persist into Q1 2024. Oil World forecasts a slight tightening in the world oils and fats dynamic in the second half of 2024. Despite overall optimism, MPOC anticipates palm oil prices to trade lower in January, between RM3,600 and RM3,850, attributed to lukewarm demand from key importing countries and price competition from sunflower and rapeseed oil. The Malaysian Palm Oil Board (MPOB) foresees a brighter outlook for the palm oil industry in 2024, expecting CPO price to range between RM3,900 and RM4,200 per tonne. MPOB Director-General Datuk Ahmad Parveez Ghulam Kadir projects Malaysian palm oil exports to increase by 3.3% to 15.60 million tonnes in 2024 from 15.10 million tonnes in 2023, backed by palm oil demand from importing countries. The export value of palm oil and palm-based products is projected to rise by 4.3% to RM110 billion in 2024 from RM105 billion in 2023. MPOB expects production to rise by 1.1% to 18.75 million tonnes in 2024 from 18.55 million tonnes in 2023, supported by an expected increase in the mature planted area and improving labour situation. MPOB expects Malaysia's palm oil stocks to be below 2.0 million tonnes, thus stabilising the price. Hong Leong Investment Bank Research maintains 2024 and 2025 CPO price assumptions of 4,000 ringgit ($862 USD) per ton and 3,800 ringgit per ton, respectively, as it expects El Nino's impact on palm production and prices to kick in around mid-2024, and Malaysia's palm oil stockpile will likely remain above 2 million tons in January 2024. Maybank Investment Bank maintains its CPO average selling price forecast of 3,700 ringgit per ton for 2024 (below 2023's 3,810 ringgit per ton), premised on a good South American soybean harvest and anticipated lower year-on-year unit cost; it expects CPO to be off to a good start in Q1 due to the seasonally low output cycle, and to trend lower by mid-2024 in anticipation of seasonally better output in H2. Affin Hwang Investment Bank maintains its CPO average selling price assumption of 4,200 ringgit to 4,400 ringgit per ton for 2024, expecting price volatility to persist in 2024 given many uncertainties surrounding the agriculture industry and global economy, including weather impacts on crop production, global edible oil inventory, demand for edible oils (food and biofuel industry), biodiesel mandates worldwide, and changes in policies.

Date/Timestamp: 2024-03-05

Plantation Industries and Commodities Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani raised concerns about low yields in smallholder areas, which are half that of corporate estates. Replanting costs are estimated at RM20,000 per hectare or higher.

    - India's total vegetable oil import is expected to decline to 16.2 million tonnes (mt) during the 2023-24 (October-September) edible oil season against 17.06 mt in 2022-23 (IVPA).

Sudhakar Desai (CEO of Emami Agrotech Ltd and President of IVPA) added that palm oil's share in total Indian imports is expected to decline from 60% in 2022-23 to 54% due to a very low spread with soft oils, potentially dropping to 50% if the soya-palm spread continues to be zero.
