Date/Timestamp: 2024-03-06
Value: CPO 872.33 USD/tonne; PKO 1,080.00 USD/tonne
Textual Content:
- **Supply**
    - Bursa Malaysia Bhd chairman Tan Sri Abdul Wahid Omar stated that the Malaysian palm oil industry is expected to show growth in 2024 due to recovery in labour supply. According to the MPOB January 2024 report, palm oil exports are projected to grow by 3.3% to 15.60 million tonnes in 2024 (from 15.10 million tonnes in 2023).
    - Plantation and Commodities Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani announced that MPOB estimates CPO production to reach 18.75 million tonnes in 2024 versus 18.55 million tonnes in 2023, a marginal increase of about 1%, driven by improved labour market conditions and a higher number of oil palm trees maturing.
    - Sime Darby Plantation Bhd expects its 2024 production growth to rise at least 5% from last year, driven by reducing reliance on foreign labour through automation and local worker recruitment. Their Fresh Fruit Bunch (FFB) production was 8.71 million metric tons in 2023, a 6% increase from 2022, and the oil extraction rate was 21.18%, slightly up from 2022. The company has sufficient workers until 2026.
    - United Plantations Bhd (UP) vice chairman and CEO Datuk Carl Bek-Nielsen expects CPO production in Malaysia to be flat, if not somewhat declining, for the first three to four months of 2024, and not high in Indonesia. UP's average CPO yield increased to 6.11 tonne per hectare from 5.89 tonne per hectare in the previous year (Malaysian estates averaged 6.3 tonnes/ha, Indonesian estates 5.34 tonnes/ha).
    - Carl Bek-Nielsen also highlighted that annual growth rates of palm oil production are slowing, dropping by 30% on average from 2011 to 2020 compared to earlier years, with another 18% drop projected from 2024 to 2030. The yearly growth is now around 1.7 million tonnes, down from 2.9 million tonnes (2010-2020). He noted that yields will remain limited until replanting is sped up, and the total area of mature oil palm plantations in Malaysia has slightly decreased over the last three to four years.
    - Minister Johari Abdul Ghani stated that 1.5 million hectares (27%) of Malaysia's 5.7 million hectares of oil palm planted area belong to approximately 450,000 smallholders, many of whom have aging trees. He suggested that consolidating even 30% of independent smallholders could add 250,000 ha to be managed more efficiently, boosting production and yields.
    - The local replanting rate remained low at 1.8% annually between 2014 and 2023, compared to industry best practices of 4.0-5.0%. By 2027, over 560,000 hectares of oil palm trees will be over 25 years old, which would lead to lower future production. Johari believes that if smallholders adopt good management practices of large plantations, FFB yield could increase by two tonnes per hectare, leading to an additional 600,000 tonnes of CPO per year (valued at RM2.4 billion at current market price) without additional land use change. The government's budget for replanting was RM100 million in the last fiscal year, covering only 5,900 ha.
    - Deputy Plantation and Commodities Minister Datuk Chan Foong Hin announced that the government will invest RM60 million to develop an oil palm biomass collection and processing centre (CPC) in Sandakan, Sabah, in collaboration with Nextgreen Global Bhd and Kumpulan Sawit Kinabalu. The total availability of oil palm biomass in Sandakan Division is estimated at 13.04 million tonnes, comprising palm fronds (8.19 mt), palm trunks (2.53 mt), empty fruit bunches (0.87 mt), mesocarp fibre (0.92 mt), and oil palm kernel shell (0.53 mt). Sandakan Division has an oil palm planting area of 742,304 ha, with 34,016 ha for replanting, and 65 oil palm mills. Sabah has the highest number of operating oil palm mills (125 units) and the country’s second-highest palm oil cultivation area (1.51 million ha) in 2023, as well as 10 palm kernel-crushing plants and 11 refineries. MPOB is also developing a palm oil biomass database system under the 12th Malaysia Plan.
- **Demand**
    - Minister Johari Abdul Ghani reported strong demand from top export destinations, with India at 17.4% of the share, China at 9.1%, and the European Union at 7.4%. This demand is supported by interest in replenishing stocks to ensure food security.
    - India's palm oil imports in February plunged 35.6% month-on-month to 504,000 metric tons, reaching a nine-month low, as higher prices prompted buyers to switch to cheaper sunflower oil. Rajesh Patel, managing partner at GGN Research, cited persistently negative margins and competitive pricing of soybean and sunflower oil.
    - India's total edible oil imports in February fell to 973,000 tonnes, the lowest in nearly two years, down 18.4% from the previous month. India buys palm oil mainly from Indonesia, Malaysia, and Thailand.
    - The Malaysian Palm Oil Council chairman, Carl Bek-Nielsen, expects Asia and Africa to absorb any palm oil supply displaced by export disruptions to Europe after the bloc's new deforestation laws. EU imports of palm oil dropped about 5% last year, but increasing demand in Asia and Africa (due to rising population) is expected to offset this loss. Last year, Africa accounted for 16% of Malaysian palm oil and oil palm product exports.
- **Policy & Trade**
    - The World Trade Organization (WTO) dispute panel largely ruled in the European Union's favour in a dispute with Malaysia over rules affecting the EU's consumption of palm oil-based biofuels. Malaysia challenged EU measures (EU Renewable Energy Directive of 2018 - RED II) limiting crop-based biofuels towards renewable energy targets and phasing out palm oil-based biofuels by 2030, which the EU deemed unsustainable due to deforestation concerns.
    - However, the WTO panel identified certain deficiencies in how the EU's measures had been prepared, published, and administered. Malaysia's Minister Johari Abdul Ghani stated this ruling demonstrates Malaysia's claims of discrimination are justified and Malaysia will monitor EU's adjustments and pursue compliance proceedings if necessary. One panel member voted in favour of Malaysia.
    - The Malaysian Palm Oil Certification Council (MPOCC) will be renamed the Malaysian Sustainable Palm Oil (MSPO) Certification to eliminate confusion with the Malaysian Palm Oil Council (MPOC).
    - Minister Johari Abdul Ghani emphasized that multilateral engagements are vital to counter negative perceptions against palm oil and that the industry must fight "unjustified negative perception" against palm oil. He also suggested encouraging big players to invest in supporting nearby smallholders to ensure the sustainability of the palm oil sector.
    - Carl Bek-Nielsen criticized the EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR), stating it may "amputate" millions of smallholders from the supply chain because they lack tracking systems and struggle with aging trees/declining yields. He suggested delaying the regulations until they are made more inclusive for smallholders, who make up 35-45% of production in Indonesia and Malaysia, and up to 90% in Thailand.
- **Substitutes & Energy**
    - Crude palm oil (CPO) imports are being offered at about US$965 a metric tonne, including cost, insurance and freight (CIF), in India for April delivery. Soyoil is offered around $950 a tonne, and sunflower oil around $928 a tonne.
    - India's sunflower oil imports surged 34% last month to 295,000 tonnes due to lower prices and as shipments originally expected in January arrived in February due to delays caused by Houthi attacks on Red Sea shipping lanes.
    - Soyoil imports in February fell 7.9% to 174,000 tonnes from a month earlier, and were far below the monthly average imports of 306,000 tonnes seen in the last marketing year ended Oct 31. India imports soyoil and sunflower oil from Argentina, Brazil, Russia, and Ukraine.
- **Market & Technicals**
    - Lower palm oil purchases by India could weigh on benchmark Malaysian palm oil futures. Falling stocks have lifted palm oil prices above rival oils, whose supplies are abundant.
    - The benchmark CPO futures for May delivery was trading at RM3,942 per tonne at 5pm on Bursa Malaysia Derivatives.
    - Bursa Malaysia Derivatives’ Crude Palm Oil Futures (FCPO) contract recorded a trading volume of 14.8 million contracts (equivalent to 370 million metric tonnes) for the entire 2023.
- **Forward Views**
    - United Plantations Bhd (UP) expects crude palm oil (CPO) prices to range between RM3,850 and RM4,250 per tonne in 2024 amid supply constraints, with production not expected to be very strong in the first three to four months.
    - Carl Bek-Nielsen, chairman of the Malaysian Palm Oil Council, also forecasted palm oil prices to hold in a range of RM3,800 to RM4,250 a tonne this year, underpinned by supply shortages and strong demand for the tropical oil.
    - Bursa Malaysia Bhd chairman Tan Sri Abdul Wahid Omar warned that while the palm oil industry’s outlook appears positive, market participants should remain vigilant of possible interlocking challenges such as unpredictable weather, potential shifts in global trade and ESG policies, and ongoing geopolitical risks.
    - Minister Johari Abdul Ghani expects the sector's outlook to remain positive in 2024. He stated that the industry and smallholders must focus on producing high-quality and high-yielding FFB and CPO sustainably.

Date/Timestamp: 2024-03-07
Value: CPO 877.00 USD/tonne; PKO 1,100.00 USD/tonne
Textual Content:
- **Supply**
    - Leading industry analyst Thomas Mielke (Oil World) indicated that annual growth of palm oil production in 2023/24 is expected to be the smallest in four years, at around 0.2 million to 0.3 million metric tons, mainly due to stagnating output from Indonesia and Malaysia. Output from Central America and Africa is seen moderately higher.
    - Mielke noted that palm oil inventories are low in Indonesia and declining in Malaysia.
    - Analyst Dorab Mistry stated that Indonesia's 2024 palm oil production will be at least one million tons lower than 2023, and Malaysia's production is likely to be unchanged. He cited inability to expand acreage, adverse tree age profiles, falling Fresh Fruit Bunch (FFB) yields, and slow technology adoption in the palm industry as concerning factors. Datuk Nageeb Wahab (Council of Palm Oil Producing Countries - CPOPC) echoed that Indonesia's production isn't growing fast enough and Malaysia's has plateaued.
    - Fastmarkets Palm Oil Analytics managing editor Dr Sathia Varqa anticipates a high phase of palm oil output from March onwards.
    - CIMB Investment Bank’s Ivy Ng Lee Fang projected global palm oil supply growth to slow to 1.8% in 2024, compared with the historical compound annual growth rate of 3.8%, due to the impact of El Nino, replanting activities, and aging estates. She added that El Nino's impact was minimal in the Malaysian plantation sector but higher in Indonesia, particularly expected in Q3 2024.
    - The Indonesia Palm Oil Association (GAPKI) official Fadhil Hasan projected Indonesia's palm oil output to rise by 2.26% to 54.4 million tonnes in 2024, with end-2024 palm oil stock estimated at 5.25 million tonnes. He said El Nino's impact on 2024 production turned out to be insignificant as it hit mostly Java and southern regions of Sumatra, which are not palm oil producing centers.
    - Hong Leong Investment Bank Research (HLIB Research) stated that most planters expect CPO production costs to trend down in 2024 on the back of higher productivity and lower fertiliser prices.

    - Global demand for palm oil is increasing by 3.5% annually (Datuk Nageeb Wahab, CPOPC).
    - Dr Sathia Varqa warned that if high palm oil prices are sustained, competitiveness and demand will suffer, especially with high stocks in China and India.
    - Indonesia's 2024 palm oil exports are seen at 29.50 million metric tonnes, down from 30.25 million tonnes last year, due to higher domestic consumption for biodiesel feedstock (GAPKI).
    - India is expected to increase purchases of soyoil in 2024, while palm oil purchases may decline, potentially keeping inventories high in Indonesia and Malaysia and impacting benchmark futures (Abdul Rasheed JanMohammad, Westbury Group).
    - Pakistan, which used to import 95% of its palm oil from Malaysia, now opts for Indonesia due to cheaper prices (Abdul Rasheed JanMohammad).
    - HLIB Research cited the absence of a notable demand catalyst for the plantation sector. Prospects for downstream players are expected to remain subdued in the near term due to overcapacity of refineries in Indonesia, a weak global economy, high inventory levels held by customers, and geopolitical tensions.
- **Policy & Trade**
    - A World Trade Organization (WTO) adjudicating panel largely rejected Malaysia's claims against the EU's decision to phase out palm oil-based biofuels by 2030 (EU Renewable Energy Directive of 2018 - RED II), supporting the bloc's stance that such fuels should not count as renewable. However, the panel accepted Malaysia's complaints over how the EU's measures had been prepared, published, and administered, requiring the EU to make adjustments without withdrawing its measures.
    - Malaysia's Plantations and Commodities Minister Johari Abdul Ghani stated that the WTO report found fault with the EU’s rules on indirect land use change to ban palm oil biofuels and with the bloc's approach to notifying and consulting with other economies. Malaysia will monitor changes and pursue compliance proceedings if necessary.
    - Indonesia's new incoming government may increase the B35 mandatory bio-content blend in biodiesel to B40 in the second half of this year, with an intention to raise it to B50 after 2025 (Fadhil Hasan, GAPKI).
    - Malaysia's biodiesel production could rise in 2024 if the 20% biodiesel mandatory program is implemented in more areas (Malaysian Biodiesel Association).
    - The New Straits Times (NST) editorial highlighted that the WTO ruling backed Malaysia on the implementation aspect of the EU regulations, which the EU agreed to comply with. The editorial described the EU's actions as "raw protectionism." It urged Malaysia to work hard to find alternative markets (China, India, Africa) for the 7.4% of palm oil currently exported to the EU. Minister Johari Abdul Ghani's proposal for consolidation of smallholdings was also noted as a creative way to help the 450,000 smallholders (30-40% of the industry).
    - Datuk Nageeb Wahab suggested that instead of competing, palm oil-producing countries (Malaysia and Indonesia) should collaborate, especially as palm oil may become scarce. Thomas Mielke urged Malaysia to speed up its replanting efforts, warning the market would turn to alternatives if the aging oil palm structure is not addressed.
- **Substitutes & Energy**
    - Thomas Mielke expects the current premium of palm oil over sunflower oil and soy oil prices to disappear in the next several weeks, as their prices are also seen rising.
    - CIMB's Ivy Ng stated that Indonesia's B35 mandate will lead to a decline in palm exports, subsequently tightening the global supply of palm oil and supporting the CPO price.
- **Market & Technicals**
    - Malaysia's palm oil benchmark contract was trading at 4,042 ringgit ($854.73) on Wednesday, up 1.4% from a day earlier.
    - The benchmark Malaysian palm oil contract jumped on Wednesday to its highest since late July at 4,075 ringgit per metric ton, representing nearly a 10% gain in 2024. The market had dropped for the last two years.
- **Forward Views**
    - Thomas Mielke (Oil World) forecasts Malaysian palm oil prices to trade in the range of RM3,800 to RM4,300 in the next three months, believing prices have made their lows and will appreciate and stay well above average in 2024 and 2025 mainly due to insufficient palm oil supplies.
    - Dr Sathia Varqa (Fastmarkets Palm Oil Analytics) anticipates the current high cost of CPO is not sustainable and expects a price drop to between RM3,500 and RM3,700 in the second half of 2024, due to high palm oil output from March onwards coupled with high stocks in China and India. He believes prices are bullish for the first quarter but expected to trade lower in the second quarter.
    - CIMB Investment Bank’s Ivy Ng Lee Fang forecasts CPO to average marginally higher at RM3,900 in 2024 compared with RM3,809 in 2023. For the long term, the research house expects CPO to average RM3,500 due to increased production costs.
    - Hong Leong Investment Bank Research (HLIB Research) projects CPO to average RM4,000 per tonne this year, before easing to RM3,800 per tonne in 2025. They maintain 2024-2025 CPO price assumptions of RM4,000 per tonne and RM3,800 per tonne, respectively, expecting El Nino’s impact on palm production and prices to kick in around mid-2024. Most plantation companies reportedly shared the view that CPO prices would likely hover around RM3,700-RM4,000 per tonne in 2024.

Date/Timestamp: 2024-03-08

Textual Content:
- **Supply**
    - Stagnating palm production growth in Malaysia and Indonesia is attributed to lack of replanting, sustainability/certification schemes, and slowdown in new plantings (RHB Research).
    - Malaysia's palm oil production is forecast to be around 18.6 million tonnes this year (TA Research). Thomas Mielke (Oil World) expects Malaysian production to be virtually stagnating in 2024.

Overall cumulative edible oil ending stocks in India revealed a general declining trend from August to December 2023, signaling a likely tightening in overall supply.

    - Most planters expect Crude Palm Oil (CPO) production costs to trend down in 2024 due to higher productivity and lower fertiliser prices (RHB Research).

    - The global edible oils and fats market is projected to grow at a Compound Annual Growth Rate (CAGR) of 5.53% from US$170.362 billion in 2022 to US$248.386 billion by 2029, driven by an expanding vegan population, health concerns, and industrial uses.
    - Key catalysts for the trajectory in CPO price trends include the weather impact on US edible oil-related crops (particularly if a La Nina emerges), changes in global biofuel policies, the situation in the Black Sea and the Red Sea, changes in Indonesia’s policy, and the development of new sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) and marine biofuel policies (RHB Research).
    - Weak performance of China’s economy and a shortage of US dollars in major palm markets (Pakistan, Bangladesh, Nigeria, Iran, and Egypt) have contributed to vegetable oil prices being below expectations in 2024 (Dorab Mistry, Godrej International, cited by RHB Research).
- **Policy & Trade**
    - The U.S. exported 17,217.2 metric tons of biodiesel and biodiesel blends of B30 or greater in January (down from 55,131.8 mt in December but up from 12,908.1 mt in January 2023). Top destinations were Canada (12,227.9 mt), Peru (4,745.3 mt), and Germany (207.4 mt). The value of U.S. biodiesel exports was $24.45 million.
    - The U.S. imported 167,713.7 metric tons of biodiesel blends (B30+) in January (up from 158,044.1 mt in December and 133,036.6 mt in January 2023). Main sources were Germany (50,077 mt), Spain (42,700.4 mt), and Canada (36,051 mt). The value of U.S. biodiesel imports reached $243.91 million.
    - Currently, 20% of the total world consumption of 17 oils and fats is absorbed by the energy sector.
    - In the years ahead, there will be a slowdown in demand growth for biodiesel and hydrogenated vegetable oils, but demand for Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) will emerge. Insufficient growth in world supplies of SAF feedstocks (like used cooking oil, tallow, and other non-food feedstock) will keep dependence high for palm oil, soyoil, and rapeseed oil as feedstock for biofuel production (RHB Research).

South America is projected to show a record bumper crop of 215 million tonnes versus 196 million tonnes a year ago (TA Research, citing Oil World).
    - Thomas Mielke (Oil World) expects the current premiums of palm oil over sunflower oil and soyoil prices to narrow in the next several weeks, driven by increased prices for sunflower oil and soyoil. He believes that rising biofuels production in North and South America will support prices.

Policy & Trade:

However, this supply growth is expected to remain modest due to Indonesia’s biodiesel mandate and a weaker output forecast from Malaysia.

Cargo surveyor Intertek Testing Services (ITS) reported a larger fall of 14.2% for the same period. This weaker export performance in the first half of March capped gains in futures prices, as noted by Anilkumar Bagani.
*   Nigeria, which imports over half of its domestic palm oil demand, is expected to see local CPO prices remain high due to rising demand and sustained foreign exchange rates.

Energy ministry official Eniya Listiani Dewi stated that the distribution of palm oil-based biodiesel this year has reached around 1.2 million kilolitres. The mandatory B40 mix (40% palm oil fuel) was planned for January 1, with a transition period for fuel distributors until the end of February, and there will be no extension. Indonesia has allocated 15.6 million KL of biodiesel for distribution in 2025, up from approximately 13 million KL last year. This implementation is closely watched for its impact on demand and Indonesia's palm oil exports.

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif met Saudi Investment Minister Khalid Al-Falih and Head of the Joint Task Force for Economic Engagement Mohammad Al-Tuwaijri to discuss attracting Saudi investments and expediting initiatives in energy, infrastructure, agriculture, and technology, with opportunities under Pakistan's Special Investment Facilitation Council (SIFC).

*   On Thursday (March 20), the ringgit strengthened 0.16% against the US dollar, making the commodity more expensive for buyers holding foreign currencies.

However, the price remained in a negative trend, down 3.56% point-to-point over the last week, 3.18% over the last month, and 0.65% year-to-date.
*   The strengthening Malaysian ringgit (up 0.58% in the last week, 1.14% year-to-date) was noted as a burden for CPO prices, making the ringgit-denominated commodity more expensive for foreign currency holders.
Forward Views

*   Cardinal Stone Research reported on Wednesday (March 19) that the oil palm market is expected to maintain elevated CPO prices in the first half of 2025, driven by robust demand from biodiesel mandates, festive seasons, and geopolitical factors affecting some substitute oils. Supply improvements may temper prices in the latter half of the year.

Britannia increased prices this quarter and expects a 4-4.5% overall price rise year-on-year. Cultivated area expanded from 67 lakh hectares in 2020-21 to approximately 94 lakh hectares in 2023-24. The Solvent Extractors’ Association of India’s (SEA) Sustainable Mustard Model Farms (MMF) initiative demonstrated an average yield increase of 20-25% compared to traditional practices, with a 24% improvement recorded in 2024-25. Johor Indian Petty Traders and Small Business Association chairman D. Ravindran reported a cooking oil shortage and rising raw material costs impacting Indian snack sales in Johor, Malaysia, with supply dropping despite increased demand. Small business owners are struggling due to the ongoing shortage.

Textual Content:

POIC Sabah Sdn Bhd CEO Datuk Fredian Gan expects recent findings on EFB uses to inspire greater confidence in the biomass sector’s growth.

Indonesia's new state palm oil firm, Agrinas Palma Nusantara, is seeking joint operations to manage its vast plantations to boost output. CEO Agus Sutomo stated Agrinas currently manages 1.5 million hectares (3.7 million acres) of seized plantations, aiming for three million hectares by 2029. Current output is 5,000-6,000 metric tons/day of fresh fruit bunches, expected to reach 10,000-12,000 tons with partners. Agrinas aims to produce 415,000 tons of crude palm oil in 2025 and 1.07 million tons in 2026. Of the 1.5 million hectares, 509,644 hectares are planted, 323,748 hectares are not planted, with the rest undergoing verification. Agrinas plans a 40-45% revenue split with corporate partners and 20% with smallholder partners in joint operations to immediately increase production and reduce costs (The Edge Malaysia). For smallholders, transparent weights from the new digital weighbridge system mean fairer payments and fewer disputes (Malay Mail).
- **Policy & Trade:** Argentina temporarily eliminated export taxes on grains and their by-products on Monday, September 23, with the suspension running through the end of October or until exports reach USD7 billion. This made Argentine soyoil shipments cheaper than palm oil for buyers in Africa and India (Business Recorder). FGV Prodata Systems, the IT subsidiary of FGV Holdings Berhad, developed ProWeigher, a fully certified digital weighbridge system deployed across FGV’s 66 mills nationwide. The system achieved full certification under Malaysia’s Akta Timbang dan Sukat 1972 (Weights and Measures Act 1972) and is recognized as legal-for-trade by the National Metrology Institute of Malaysia (NMIM) and SIRIM. The system integrates advanced safeguards to prevent tampering, including QR codes and number-plate recognition for trucks, biometric logins, and TAC authorization codes for staff. Each reading is digitally encrypted, generating a secure checksum stored in a legally relevant database to ensure that fruit bunches and palm kernel deliveries cannot be under-reported or manipulated. This system is integrated into the FGV Traceability of Product (FGVTOP) platform, which tracks palm oil from plantation polygons to export consignments. This is significant for the EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR) (Malay Mail). The technology has drawn regional attention, with FGV Prodata presenting its weighbridge system to Vietnam’s National Metrology Institute as a model for digital compliance (Malay Mail). Majumder Agrotech International Ltd and Bogura Multi Oil Mills Ltd each secured approval for 10,000 tonnes. Bangladesh exported around 75,000 tonnes of rice bran oil worth approximately Tk 974 crore in the last fiscal year 2024-25 (nan).

Textual Content:
- **Supply:** Palm oil production is stagnant, and productivity growth has fallen to zero or even negative. In Indonesia, a policy of seizing "private but not fully legal plantations" is leading to a decline in productivity, and in Malaysia, palm trees are aging without proper renewal. Veteran trader Dorab Mistry called on Indonesia to lift its moratorium on new plantations. Palm oil supply growth is forecast at just 1 million tonnes in 2025/26, compared with 1.5 million tonnes a year earlier (UkrAgroConsult). Indonesia's new state palm oil firm Agrinas Palma Nusantara is seeking joint operations to boost output from its vast plantations (Reuters).

India has emerged as the leading rapeseed meal supplier to China due to Beijing’s introduction of preliminary anti-dumping duties on Canadian rapeseed imports in August, alongside previous duties imposed in March 2025 on Canadian rapeseed meal and oil, creating prohibitive tariffs on all Canadian canola products (Oils & Fats International). China’s domestic rapeseed production has been insufficient, leading it to engage with alternative trade partners; India’s rapeseed meal exports to China totaled almost 100,000 tonnes in July (Oils & Fats International). China is expected to import 2.6M tonnes of rapeseed meal in 2025/26 (400,000 tonnes higher than the previous estimate, but a three-year low). Tariffs on Canadian rapeseed imports are expected to reduce China’s total rapeseed imports due to limited eligible suppliers. China’s 2025/26 rapeseed imports are forecast at 4.1M tonnes (700,000 lower than the previous estimate, and a four-year low) without Canada and Australia (Oils & Fats International). India could increase palm oil imports to 9.3 million tonnes in 2025/26 from 8.2 million tonnes, while total vegetable oil imports would rise 5% to 17.1 million tonnes (UkrAgroConsult). New Zealand, the world’s largest palm kernel (PK) meal importer, saw its imports increase by 200,000 tonnes in 2024/25 to a record high of 2.7M tonnes. PK meal consumption is forecast to increase as national herd numbers recover slightly. New Zealand is forecast to import 2.5M tonnes of PK meal in 2025/26, down 200,000 tonnes from the previous year. Indonesia is the leading exporter of PK meal to New Zealand (~60% market share), with Malaysia as the second largest (>40% share) (Oils & Fats International). The collaboration between APOA, CPOPC, and Solidaridad aims to ensure supply stability for over 1.5 billion consumers in South Asia. Sanjeev Asthana, President of SEA, stated that the partnership strengthens India’s access to affordable, high-quality palm oil. India meets over 60% of its edible oil demand through imports, with Indonesia consistently serving as its largest palm oil supplier for over a decade. India’s palm oil imports rose nearly 16% to 9.9 lakh tonnes in August 2025 – the highest in over a year (Business Line).

The regulation was originally scheduled to take effect on December 30 (Reuters). CIMB Securities viewed the EUDR delay as slightly positive for palm oil producers, easing concerns of weaker palm oil demand in the first quarter of 2026, though it extends regulatory uncertainty (New Straits Times). If Indonesia implements the B50 standard, it will cause a shortage of palm oil (UkrAgroConsult). Australia is in discussion with China to develop a phytosanitary framework for rapeseed access after being shut out of the market since 2020 due to detections of blackleg disease (Oils & Fats International). The Asian Palm Oil Alliance (APOA), the Council of Palm Oil Producing Countries (CPOPC), and Solidaridad Network Asia Limited (SNAL) signed a tripartite Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) in Mumbai to strengthen collaboration between producers and consumers and accelerate sustainability in the palm oil value chain, focusing on India and South Asia. The MoU emphasizes regenerative practices and promotes traceable, smallholder-inclusive, and NDPE-compliant sourcing using Solidaridad’s SoliTrace digital traceability tool and complementary remote-sensing technologies. These pilots will provide mill-to-market visibility and importer-facing dashboards tailored to Indian buyers. A Joint Working Group, co-chaired by APOA and CPOPC, with Solidaridad as the Technical Secretariat, will oversee workplans and coordination. The MoU is valid for three years (Business Line).

Oil prices rose for a second day on Wednesday as an industry report showed US crude inventories declined last week, adding to a sense of tightening supplies. Stronger crude oil futures make palm oil a more attractive option for biodiesel feedstock (Reuters). Soybean, sunflower, and rapeseed crops are not expanding due to the low attractiveness of oilseed prices (UkrAgroConsult). Soybean oil could rise by more than 40% due to demand for biodiesel in the United States, reaching 70 cents per pound (UkrAgroConsult). Sunflower oil could become competitive by mid-2026, thanks to higher harvests in the Black Sea region and Argentina (UkrAgroConsult). Increased use of dried distillers grains (DDGs) as feed in India, following a higher ethanol blending rate, reduced Indian domestic rapeseed meal consumption (Oils & Fats International).

Date/Timestamp: 2025-09-26
Value: CPO 1,036.11 USD/tonne; PKO 2,115.00 USD/tonne
Textual Content:
- **Supply:** Almost half of Indonesia’s crude palm oil (CPO) output is now absorbed by the domestic market. CPO consumption rose to 23.8 million tonnes in 2024, while production fell to 52.7 million tonnes (down from 54.8 million tonnes in 2023), according to Indonesian Palm Oil Producers Association (Gapki) chairman Eddy Martono. Indonesia accounts for 57% of global CPO output and 27% of global use. Production challenges include land conflicts and the need to rejuvenate smallholder plantations, which manage around 42% of palm oil plantations in the country and currently have low annual yields (as low as 10 tonnes of fresh fruit bunches per ha). Replanting could triple these yields. Gapki urged the government to issue clear land certificates for both corporate and community plantations (The Star).
- **Demand:** The biodiesel mandate is driving up domestic use in Indonesia, with food consumption followed by energy or biodiesel demand. Indonesia is the world’s largest producer and consumer of CPO (The Star). If exports were constrained by Indonesia's domestic biodiesel program, the global vegetable oil supply could be disrupted. Indonesia’s palm oil exports weakened last year when prices rose above other vegetable oils and global buyers turned to cheaper alternatives. China and India remain the largest external markets, but shipments to India dipped through mid-2025 (down 28% year-on-year in the first half of the year) due to price sensitivity. India’s overall vegetable oil consumption has continued to climb and reached nearly 25 million tonnes annually, with imported palm oil contributing around nine million tonnes. Indonesia remains India's largest supplier of palm oil, shipping around 4.4 million tonnes of the commodity in 2024, according to Oil World (The Star). The Bangladesh government rejected a proposal by traders to raise the price of soybean oil by Tk 10 per litre. Despite this, prices of loose soybean oil and Super Palm Oil increased by around Tk 5 per litre over the past three to four days in Dhaka markets. Retail prices for loose soybean oil range from Tk 170 to Tk 172 per litre, while Super Palm Oil is selling for Tk 155 to Tk 160 per litre. Four days ago, loose soybean oil was Tk 169 per litre, and palm oil was Tk 150 per litre. Wholesalers and retailers said suppliers reduced their commission, creating a supply shortage that is pushing prices up. Wholesale rates for bottled oil increased, though retail prices fixed by the government since August 3 (Tk 189/litre for bottled soybean oil, Tk 922 for a five-litre bottle, Tk 169/litre for loose soybean oil, and Tk 150/litre for palm oil) have not changed, forcing retailers to sell at a loss. A 204-litre drum of loose soybean oil rose from Tk 32,000 to Tk 34,400, while a drum of loose Super Palm Oil increased from Tk 29,000 to Tk 31,000 (Jagonews24). A record amount of canola oil was consumed domestically in Canada during the first six months of 2025, largely due to the biofuel sector (The Western Producer). Canada recently lost a five million tonne market for canola seed when China slapped a 75.8% import duty on the crop (The Western Producer).
- **Policy & Trade:** Gapki chairman Eddy Martono stressed the priority of supplying Indonesia's local biodiesel and food industries but urged striking a balance between domestic supply and exports (The Star). The Malaysian Palm Oil Council (MPOC) welcomed the European Union’s decision to delay the implementation of its EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR) by 12 months to December 2026, but cautioned that the regulation remains unworkable without a clear implementation pathway and creates an unsustainable burden for responsible businesses due to a lack of clarity (Business Today). MPOC criticized the EU’s risk classification system for placing Malaysia under a “standard risk” category despite Malaysia’s superior environmental performance, including a 57% reduction in primary forest loss between 2015–2017 and 2020–2022, a 13% further decline in 2024, and falling out of the top 10 countries for tropical primary forest loss for the first time. Malaysia enforces the Malaysian Sustainable Palm Oil (MSPO) 2022 standard, which prohibits the conversion of natural forests, protected zones, and high conservation value areas after December 31, 2019. MPOC urged the EU to use the extended timeline to reform the EUDR’s classification framework to reflect measurable environmental outcomes, recognize countries with proven forest conservation results, and provide a clear pathway for countries to improve their classifications (Business Today). The Bangladesh Vegetable Oil Refiners and Vanaspati Manufacturers Association had requested a Tk 10/litre price hike; the commerce ministry decided to allow a Tk 1/litre increase after a meeting on Monday, but no formal announcement was made by refining and marketing companies (Jagonews24). Chris Vervaet, executive director of the Canadian Oilseed Processors Association (COPA), stated that 64% of the renewable diesel consumed in Canada in 2024 was made from either tallow or used cooking oil (UCO), and that COPA is lobbying the federal government to amend its Clean Fuel Regulations (CFR) to prevent imported UCO-based biofuel from collecting biofuel credits, which would level the playing field for competing feedstocks (The Western Producer). Canada imported 692 million litres of biodiesel in 2024 and exported 514 million litres to the United States to collect the blender’s tax credit, which was replaced by the 45Z Clean Fuel Production Credit in 2025 (ineligible for Canadian biofuel), meaning more Canadian biodiesel will be consumed domestically. Most renewable diesel used in Canada was imported (1.03 billion litres) due to lack of domestic production (The Western Producer). British Columbia and Ontario have implemented domestic content requirements in their provincial regulations, and Ottawa has signalled that the federal CFR will be amended to enhance the viability of domestic producers (The Western Producer). Fred Ghatala, president of Advanced Biofuels Canada, noted that Canada’s CFR adds $1.09 per bushel to canola prices (The Western Producer).
- **Substitutes & Energy:** Canola oil accounted for 21% of the feedstock for biodiesel and 24% of the feedstock for renewable diesel used in Canada in 2024. Canada used 449 million litres of biodiesel and 1.46 billion litres of renewable diesel in 2024, requiring an estimated 930,000 tonnes of canola seed for these uses. There are suspicions that some imported UCO-based biofuel is mislabelled palm oil biofuel, which has sustainability concerns due to deforestation associated with palm plantations, but there is no way to test the fuel for composition (The Western Producer). New renewable diesel production facilities, Braya Renewable Fuels in Newfoundland and Labrador (opened April 2024) and Imperial Oil in Strathcona, Alta. (opened August 2025), each capable of producing one billion litres annually, are expected to increase domestic production (The Western Producer).
- **Market & Technicals:** Singapore-based global palm oil company Wilmar International was found guilty of corruption by Indonesia’s Supreme Court, overturning its previous acquittal in a graft case involving cooking oil export permits during the 2021-2022 shortage crisis. Two Indonesian palm oil companies, Permata Hijau and Musim Mas, also had their acquittals overturned. The companies were accused of illegally profiting from the evasion of state-imposed export controls. The Indonesian Attorney-General’s Office (AGO) has sought 11.8 trillion rupiah (S$906 million) in compensation and a billion rupiah fine from Wilmar; Permata Hijau faced a fine of one billion rupiah and was ordered to pay 937 billion rupiah in compensation; Musim Mas was fined one billion rupiah and ordered to pay 4.8 trillion rupiah in compensation. Wilmar's share price tumbled 3.1%, or nine cents, to $2.80 (The Straits Times).

However, CPO output fell 14% to 13,320 tonnes (from 15,476 tonnes) and PK volume declined 15% to 2,789 tonnes (from 3,300 tonnes). Compared to 2Q2025, WTK recorded a 2% increase in FFB production to 67,459 tonnes (from 66,363 tonnes), a 1% rise in CPO output to 13,320 tonnes (from 13,137 tonnes), and a 6% growth in PK output to 2,789 tonnes (from 2,622 tonnes). For 9M2025, WTK’s FFB production rose 11% to 195,149 tonnes (from 175,102 tonnes in 9M2024), CPO production fell 8% to 38,581 tonnes (from 41,900 tonnes), and PK production dipped 10% to 8,004 tonnes (from 8,882 tonnes). **Demand**
Malaysia is exploring South Africa as a potential regional hub for its palm oil exports to the African market, following discussions between Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Tengku Datuk Seri Zafrul Tengku Abdul Aziz and South African Minister of Trade, Industry and Competition Parks Tau.
**Policy & Trade**
US President Donald Trump signed an Agreement on Reciprocal Trade with Malaysia's Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim. US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer stated Malaysia will modify its tariffs and non-tariff barriers, expecting agriculture, technology, and services sectors to benefit. Under the agreement, Malaysia will provide significant preferential market access for US agricultural exports, chemicals, machinery, electrical equipment, metals, and passenger vehicles, and address barriers for digital trade, services, and investment. Malaysia will not ban or impose quotas on critical minerals or rare earth elements exports to the US, and committed to their expeditious development with US companies, including extended operating licenses.
Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Tengku Datuk Seri Zafrul Abdul Aziz announced that 1,711 Malaysian export products to the US will enjoy tariffs lower than 19%. This list, amounting to about US$5.2 billion (RM21.96 billion) or 12% of Malaysia's total exports to the US, includes palm oil, rubber, cocoa, some pharmaceutical components, and aerospace equipment. These lower tariffs will take effect within 60 days after documents are exchanged. The US identified products under Annex III to Executive Order 14346 (Sept 5, 2025) to receive a 0% reciprocal tariff rate, while committing to maintain 19% reciprocal tariffs (first outlined in Executive Order 14257, April 2, 2025) on other originating goods of Malaysia. Zafrul expressed satisfaction with the deal, noting Malaysia did not backtrack and gained better access than previously discussed verbally. Trump had set a 19% tariff on Malaysia in August, lower than the 25% threatened in July. Trade between the two countries totaled nearly US$87 billion last year. Malaysia had been negotiating for less onerous US trade conditions and is negotiating to be spared from tariffs on semiconductor imports to the US, its third-largest market for chips.
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent was in Kuala Lumpur for talks with Chinese Vice-Premier He Lifeng ahead of an expected meeting between Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping.
Discussions between Malaysia and South Africa included strengthening collaboration in key sectors like electric vehicles (EVs), halal industry development, and industrial partnerships, with follow-up working groups to be established.
**Forward Views**
US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer expects the agriculture, technology, and services sectors to benefit from the new trade agreement with Malaysia. Dan Kritenbrink, a partner at the Asia Group, expects the trade deal with Malaysia to encourage and pressure other deals in the region. The Malaysian government expects economic growth to slow to 4%-4.5% in 2026, from a projected expansion of as much as 4.8% in 2025, after the economy expanded 5.2% in 3Q2025.
The Malaysian Palm Oil Board (MPOB) will host the MPOB International Palm Oil Congress and Exhibition (PIPOC 2025) at the Kuala Lumpur Convention Centre (KLCC) from November 18 to 20, 2025. The event is expected to convene over 2,000 delegates, 100 international speakers, 200 poster presentations, and over 400 exhibitors, including leading plantation groups like SD Guthrie Berhad, FGV Holdings Berhad, Genting Plantations, Sarawak Plantation Berhad, and United Plantations Berhad, to showcase innovations across the oil palm value chain. MPOB Director General Datuk Dr Ahmad Parveez Ghulam Kadir stated the exhibition embodies the full journey of the oil palm industry from plantation to product innovation, with the MPOB Pavilion highlighting the organization's Six R&D Focus Areas.

Ghana cultivates approximately 300,000 hectares of oil palm, producing around 300,000 metric tonnes of crude palm oil annually. Exports of Malaysian palm oil products for October 1-25 were seen to fall between 0.3% (AmSpec Agri Malaysia and Intertek Testing Services) and 0.4% (Intertek Testing Services) from the amount shipped during September 1-25. Intertek Testing Services specified a fall of 0.4% to 1,283,814 metric tons from 1,288,462 metric tons. Nepal's exports to India surged by nearly 138% during the first quarter of the current fiscal year 2025–26, driven significantly by processed soybean oil exports worth NPR 30.69 billion (52% of total exports to India). Processed sunflower seed oil ranked second with NPR 2.13 billion, while palm oil stood third with NPR 1.73 billion in exports. Indonesia’s palm oil export revenue rose sharply by 43% year-on-year to $24.79 billion in the January-August 2025 period. Export volume increased by 15% to 22.69 million tons (from 19.68 million tons a year earlier). Higher exports were recorded across several major destination markets, including Malaysia, China, Africa, the European Union, Russia, and the United States. The average CPO price between January and August stood at $1,204 per ton, higher than the $1,009 per ton average recorded over the same period last year. Palm oil exports from Indonesia totaled 3.47 million tonnes in August 2025, a 1.8% decrease from July. The US is China’s top market for used cooking oil, exporting $1.1 billion last year, which was a fraction of the $12.6 billion China spent importing US soybeans.
**Policy & Trade**
Malaysian Palm Oil Board (MPOB) director general Datuk Dr Ahmad Parveez Ghulam Kadir stated that the US decision to lower tariffs to below 19% on 1,711 Malaysian export products, including palm oil and cocoa products, will enhance their price competitiveness in the US market. This move grants lower tariffs for palm oil and palm kernel oil products, as well as palm-based oleochemical derivatives (fatty acids, fatty alcohols, and Vitamin A and E), which will lower landed costs and spur downstream exports. Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Tengku Datuk Seri Zafrul Abdul Aziz previously stated these products amount to about US$5.2 billion (RM21.9 billion), or 12% of Malaysia's total exports to the US. The lower tariffs are expected to take effect within 60 days after document exchange. The US identified products under Annex III to Executive Order 14346 (Sept 5, 2025) for a 0% reciprocal tariff rate, and committed to maintain 19% reciprocal tariffs (Executive Order 14257, April 2, 2025) on other Malaysian goods.

The Tree Crop Development Authority (TCDA) outlined measures, including strict enforcement of traceability systems and mandatory registration for transporters. OPDAG called for stronger collaboration among regulatory agencies (Ghana Revenue Authority, FDA, GSA, National Security) and firm penalties for offenders.

SMARTRI models estimate drought-related productivity losses cost Indonesia’s palm oil industry over US$4.5 billion annually, with yields potentially declining 8-10% for every 100mm water deficit and up to 21% in high-risk regions like Lampung. The Malaysian palm oil industry adheres to zero-waste principles, converting agricultural waste such as empty fruit bunches (EFB), fibre, shells, and palm oil mill effluent (POME) into useful resources like fertiliser and fuel, which prevents carbon emissions from decomposition. This effort aligns with Malaysia's goal to achieve net zero emissions by 2050 and UN Sustainable Development Goals 7, 12, and 13. The Malaysian Palm Oil Council (MPOC), in collaboration with Swinburne University of Technology (Sarawak campus), published a study in November 2024 outlining a roadmap for the industry to reach carbon neutrality. Current practices like combined heat and power systems and biogas capture from POME have led to a 68.8% reduction in the industry’s greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions by replacing fossil fuels and avoiding methane. Emerging technologies include converting EFB into briquettes/pellets for renewable energy, biochar via pyrolysis for soil aeration and carbon storage, synthetic gas via gasification, and bioethanol via fermentation. Challenges to large-scale implementation include the need for more R&D, collaborative efforts, expanded local manufacturing of equipment (e.g., high-pressure steam generators, anaerobic digestion components are imported), efficient biomass collection/transport/storage, consistent material quality, good infrastructure, and substantial capital injection.

The Malaysian Palm Oil Green Conservation Foundation (MPOGCF) unveiled a 94-page "Panduan Pengecaman Tapak Hidupan Liar di Lapangan" (Field guide to the identification of wildlife tracks).

Date/Timestamp: 2025-11-27
Value: CPO 971.00 USD/tonne; PKO 1,875.00 USD/tonne
Textual Content:
- **Supply**
  - Malaysia’s October output jumped 11%, the strongest since August 2015, pushing stockpiles to a six-and-a-half-year high. Budiman Suwardi, head of treasury and markets at Borneo Agri-Resources International, stated this inventory build-up resulted in an overhang and would be a key fundamental drag on palm oil prices.
  - Genting Plantations expects fresh fruit bunch (FFB) production to ease in the remaining months of the year after peaking in October across its Malaysian and Indonesian estates, anticipating full-year 2025 output to be marginally lower year-on-year. FFB production in 3Q25 declined year-on-year due to a low cropping trend at several estates, persistent heavy rainfall and flooding in 1Q25, and ongoing replanting activities.
  - Sarawak Oil Palms Bhd’s net profit for 3QFY2025 declined 8.91% to RM110.95 million (versus RM121.81 million a year earlier) due to higher production costs and lower contribution from refined palm products, although partially cushioned by improved FFB yields. Revenue slipped 3.33% to RM1.34 billion (from RM1.38 billion) due to lower average selling prices of crude palm oil (CPO) and palm kernel products. YTD net profit grew 3.15% to RM316.63 million (from RM306.95 million), as YTD revenue rose 6.18% to RM4.08 billion (from RM3.85 billion).
  - UkrAgroConsult reported a seasonal increase in the supply of vegetable oils.
  - The national replanting rate in Malaysia stands at about 1.5%, significantly below the 4.0% required, leaving a backlog of roughly 650,000 hectares of palms over 25 years old. MPOB simulations show that replanting 200,000–228,000 ha annually could eliminate this backlog within four to five years and lift national yields from 17.9 tonnes per ha to 20.8 tonnes per ha by 2035.
  - Indonesia's Agriculture Minister Andi Amran Sulaiman criticized the discovery of 2.04 tonnes of illegally imported cooking oil in Batam.
  - Genting Plantations acquired an Indonesian oil palm seed producer, strengthening its seed development capabilities and expanding its reach to growers. Its AgTech segment uses AI, big data, and genomic research to develop high-yielding, disease-resistant planting materials.
- **Demand**
  - Palm oil prices remained under pressure due to softer export demand. Early estimates pointed to a 14%-20% month-on-month drop in exports during the first 20 days of November. Cargo surveyor data for Nov 1-25 was awaited. UkrAgroConsult reported a 16.5% decline in palm oil exports from Malaysia between November 1 and 25 compared to the same period in October.
  - Expectations that India, the world’s largest buyer, could boost palm oil purchases by about 20% in the next marketing year amid more competitive pricing.
  - EU palm oil imports continue to decline, dropping about 20% to nearly 958,000 tonnes between July 1-November 2, 2025, compared to the same period last year (EU Commission figures reported by UFOP). Malaysia remained the leading supplier (272,000 tonnes, 28% of total, a slight increase in exports), while Indonesia ranked second (261,000 tonnes, a sharp decline). The Netherlands remained the leading hub (353,000 tonnes, ~12% increase), followed by Italy (303,000 tonnes, an 8% decrease). Greece recorded the sharpest decline (-91%), followed by Sweden (-37%) and Denmark (-30%). Germany imported 78,000 tonnes, down 13%. Belgium and Spain slightly increased import volumes.
  - Reduced demand from the biofuel industry was noted by UkrAgroConsult.
  - China exported a record 70,877 thousand tons of soybean oil in October, mostly to India; total exports for ten months of 2025 reached 329 thousand tons, almost three times higher than the figures for the whole of last year.
- **Policy & Trade**
  - Malaysia’s Palm Oil Board set a lower crude palm oil reference price for December.
  - Indonesia’s Trade Minister Budi Santoso said CPO exports remain stable ahead of the B50 biodiesel mandate rollout in 2026. The B50 program aims to eliminate Indonesia’s remaining diesel imports, projected at 4.9 million kiloliters in 2025. The Energy Ministry estimates biodiesel use between 2020 and 2025 has saved $40.7 billion in foreign exchange, with B50 expected to add another $10.8 billion in savings in its first year.
  - The decline in EU palm oil imports is due to the exclusion of palm oil-based biofuels from national quota obligations and an increase in imports of waste oils and fats for transport fuel production. UFOP stated such exclusions must be implemented across the entire EU by 2030, and welcomed the planned abolition of double counting for waste oils/fats.
  - Genting Plantations' palm-based biodiesel will primarily serve the Malaysian biodiesel mandate, with limited export opportunities. Its downstream manufacturing segment expects intense competition from Indonesian producers and refinery overcapacity.
  - CIMB Securities highlighted that clear policies, particularly on biodiesel, are crucial for a sustained price recovery, and price behavior has been largely driven by shifting expectations around Indonesia's B40–B50 biodiesel mandates and the US Environmental Protection Agency (EPA).
  - The Plantation and Commodities Ministry (KPK) plans to request membership to the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) to provide a fact-based narrative of the palm oil industry’s sustainable practices in Malaysia. KPK deputy secretary-general Datuk Razali Mohamad reported over RM10 million is spent annually on conservation programmes such as replanting and wildlife protection by smallholders. A 94-page "Panduan Pengecaman Tapak Hidupan Liar di Lapangan" (Field guide to the identification of wildlife tracks) was unveiled.
- **Substitutes & Energy**
  - CPO futures closed lower, tracking weaker soybean oil prices.
  - Weaker contracts on China’s Dalian exchange added to downward pressure. Dalian's most-active soyoil contract was up 0.07%, while its palm oil contract shed 0.47%.
  - Soyoil prices on the Chicago Board of Trade were up 0.12%. Soybean oil for January in Chicago rose 0.3% to 50.7c/lb.
  - January Brent crude futures fell 3.8% to $62.5/barrel in the week (-3.8% in the month), contributing to lower palm oil prices.
  - December soybean oil futures in Chicago fell 3.8% to $1,108/tonne in the week (-1% in the month).
  - The price of soybean oil in Brazil increased by $10/t to $1,110-1,120/t FOB in a week, but the price of soybean oil in China fell by $10/t to $1,160-1,165/t Daylian. Chinese soybean oil is $10-15/t cheaper than Brazilian oil in the Indian market, with delivery taking 10-12 days versus 50-60 days.
  - China's commercial soybean oil stocks topped 1 million tons as of mid-November (a seven-year high), due to falling consumption (fewer restaurants, slowing economy) and excess supply of cheap Brazilian soybeans. China is obligated to buy an additional 12 million tons from the United States by the end of 2025.
  - Sunflower oil prices delivered to India remained at $1,300-1,310/t CIF Mumbai. Russian sunflower oil increased by $10-20/t to $1,200-1,210/t FOB for November-December delivery. Demand prices for sunflower oil in Ukraine remained at $1,220–1,230/t for delivery to ports in November–December, but supply increased amid reduced demand from EU buyers due to euro depreciation.
  - Rapeseed oil prices in the EU fell by $10-15/t to $1,260-1,265/t FOB Netherlands over the week amid increased rapeseed supply and lower oil prices. Increased supplies of canola oil from Canada and Australia are expected in the coming months.
  - Weaker crude oil futures make palm a less attractive option for biodiesel feedstock. Oil prices were little changed, with concerns that supply will exceed demand next year outweighing worries about Russian shipments.
  - Soybean oil’s premium over palm was ~$133 (RM551.02)/tonne versus an average of ~$70 in the past year. Palm’s premium over gasoil was ~$271/tonne versus an average of ~$316 in the past year.
- **Market & Technicals**
  - Malaysian palm oil futures inched higher on Tuesday after three straight sessions of losses, with the benchmark contract for February delivery gaining RM11, or 0.27%, to RM4,066 (US$984.98) a metric ton by 0232 GMT.
  - Benchmark palm oil climbed 0.23% to 3,999 ringgit ($967.5) per tonne on November 26, rebounding slightly after sliding more than 8.5% over the past month and down nearly 17% from a year earlier. Futures in Kuala Lumpur hovered near 4,025 ringgit, touching their weakest level since late June.
  - The ringgit strengthened 0.24% against the dollar on Tuesday. A firmer ringgit continued to dampen export appetite, making the commodity more expensive for buyers.
  - December palm oil futures FCPO1 fell 1.6% to 3,990 ringgit/t or $965/t over the week, falling below the psychological level of 4,000 ringgit/tonne. The futures contract for February delivery on the Bursa Malaysia Derivatives Exchange rose as much as 0.7% to RM4,097/tonne, standing at RM4,083/tonne at midday break, down 8% year to date.
  - Total volume climbed to 73,960 lots from 70,608 lots on Friday, while open interest increased to 288,313 contracts from 287,400 contracts previously. The physical CPO price for December South narrowed by RM20 to RM4,080 per tonne.
  - Asian share markets rallied as hopes grew that the Federal Reserve will deliver a December interest rate cut.
- **Forward Views**
  - Market players expect the rise in palm prices to be capped by expectations of growing supply.
  - Genting Plantations anticipates palm products prices to remain firm in the near term, supported by tight palm oil supply and resilient biodiesel demand underpinned by ongoing mandates. However, subdued demand due to unfavorable price spread against other edible oils and absence of festive demand, amid trade policy uncertainties, may limit price upside.
  - CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd expects CPO prices to remain range-bound in the near term, trading between RM4,000 and RM4,600 per tonne in the first half of 2026. Short-term price swings may persist, with prices likely volatile within RM4,000–4,300 per tonne without decisive policy signals. Their average CPO price forecasts are RM4,330 per tonne for 2025 and RM4,200 per tonne for 2026. A cautiously constructive outlook points to a potential recovery to RM4,300–RM4,400 per tonne by Q1 next year if export demand improves and palm oil becomes more competitive against soybean oil, though sustained upside will still require clear policy catalysts.
  - Sarawak Oil Palms’ outlook will remain influenced by supply chain pressures on fertiliser, chemical and fuel costs, FFB production, and global edible oil prices.
  - Reuters technical analyst Wang Tao said palm oil may bounce into a range of RM4,102 to RM4,145 per ton, following its stabilization around support of 4,034 ringgit.

Date/Timestamp: 2025-11-28
Value: CPO 971.00 USD/tonne; PKO 1,730.00 USD/tonne
Textual Content:
- **Supply**
  - Two Village Unit Cooperatives (KUDs) partnering with Asian Agri signed a Cooperation Agreement for the Smallholder Palm Oil Replanting Programme (PSR) in Riau, Indonesia, in collaboration with the Palm Oil Plantation Fund Management Agency (BPDPKS) and participating banks. KUD Sejahtera (Pelalawan Regency) covers 179 hectares with 78 smallholders, and KUD Kebun Sawit Harapan (Siak Regency) spans 219 hectares with 95 smallholders. Normansyah Hidayat Syahruddin, Director of Upstream Fund Distribution at BPDPKS, emphasized responsible fund utilization. The program is a key strategy to restore yields in aging plantations and promote land-use efficiency. Palm trees take about seven years to reach full maturity.
  - Plantation and Commodities Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani stated that Malaysia, as the world’s second-largest producer, has produced 19.4 million tonnes of palm oil, compared to Indonesia's 50 million tonnes.
  - The minister noted that floods occurring nationwide did not affect palm oil production, but he expressed concern for smallholders.
  - Malaysia is focused on increasing palm oil yield, using good planting material, and avoiding deforestation. The industry is shifting towards responsible and efficient practices rather than land expansion, concentrating on improving yields through better planting materials and stronger agricultural practices.
- **Demand**
  - Malaysia’s palm oil exports to China fell by almost 29% (The Star Online) or nearly 39% (New Straits Times, The Malaysian Reserve, The Sun) in the first 10 months of 2025, primarily due to palm oil trading at a higher price than soybean oil. Exports to China totalled 1.39 million metric tons last year, down 5.3% from a year earlier.
  - Chinese buyers, who collectively account for roughly 2.5 million tonnes of China's palm oil requirements, opted for the cheaper soybean oil alternative.
  - Plantation and Commodities Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani advised Chinese palm oil buyers to negotiate with Malaysian industry players to enjoy better palm oil prices, suggesting discounts for one-year purchase commitments. He also urged Chinese companies to establish a presence in Malaysia through partnerships with local investors.
- **Policy & Trade**
  - The Plantation and Commodities Ministry (KPK) advised Chinese buyers to commit to long-term palm oil deals for better pricing. Johari suggested that major Malaysian plantation companies, collectively producing about 19.4 to 19.5 million tonnes annually, could explore offering discounts for one-year supply commitments instead of spot purchases.
  - The Malaysian Palm Oil Council (MPOC) hosted a trade networking visit for 37 prominent Chinese palm oil buyers from November 25–27, 2025, which included site visits to plantation and refinery facilities.
  - Johari emphasized Malaysia's commitment to upholding transparent and predictable export policies and welcomed continuous dialogue with trading partners.
  - He confirmed that US tariffs have no impact on palm oil, and any other US trade measures do not affect Malaysian palm oil supply to China. Malaysian trade flows with China remain stable and uninterrupted.
  - Johari encouraged Chinese companies to consider deeper investments in Malaysia, particularly in technology-driven segments across the upstream, midstream, and downstream value chains, proposing joint ventures with Malaysian investors.
  - The sector is moving towards a circular economy model, ensuring that plantation by-products are reused. Empty fruit bunches are now widely used as feedstock for renewable energy and for the production of bio-based products. Palm oil mill effluent and used cooking oil are increasingly channeled into advanced biofuel production, including sustainable aviation fuel (SAF).
  - Eco Ceres, a Hong Kong-based biofuels producer with a 350,000 tonnes processing capacity, had its first SAF shipment from Johor and stated that it would take all palm oil and used cooking oil Malaysia can supply.
- **Substitutes & Energy**
  - The decline in Malaysia’s palm oil exports to China was attributed to palm oil becoming more expensive than soybean oil, with the price difference between the two commodities reaching around US$120 per tonne at one point.
  - Crude palm oil prices were consistently above RM4,200 and at one point trading at a premium of around US$120 (RM495.7) over soybean oil.
  - Johari expects the palm-soybean price spread to normalize, contributing to the palm oil sector's stability.
- **Market & Technicals**
  - Malaysia's crude palm oil futures on the Bursa Malaysia Derivatives Exchange were trading at RM4,060 per tonne on Thursday.
- **Forward Views**
  - Plantation and Commodities Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani expects palm prices to remain above 4,000 ringgit per metric ton by the end of the year and expressed optimism about palm oil exports to China next year, believing the palm-soybean price spread would normalize. He remains bullish on the palm oil sector into 2026, expecting CPO price above RM4,000/tonne to be safe, underpinned by Malaysia's sustainability focus, circular economy practices, and growing downstream opportunities such as renewable energy and sustainable aviation fuel.
